items.title: I contemplated suicide at height of Man United career, Rooney reveals
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Wayne Rooney has revealed he contemplated suicide during the height of his Manchester United career, despite success on the pitch and major milestones in his personal life. Speaking on the Life At The Midpoint with Gabby Logan podcast, the former England captain said he struggled with his mental health, spent two days at a time drinking at home and withdrew from people around him. “I can look back and say I was selfish, but I knew I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with,” Rooney said. “Then I didn’t want Kai seeing me like that, so that’s why I’d hide away as well. “I got to a place where you’re contemplating suicide. You just didn’t want to be around anyone. I didn’t want to see people in the streets. I didn’t want to go into shops. “I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else (I) really struggled with it.” Rooney, Manchester United’s all-time record goalscorer with 253 goals, said he found it difficult to admit he was struggling because he feared it would be seen as a sign of weakness. “You don’t want to show any weakness, so you try to mask it,” he said. “Even though I knew the position I was in, it was difficult to actually admit that I was in that position because I felt like you feel less of a man if you like for doing that. “I was speaking to a therapist to try and figure out what was up with me because, when I look back, I was probably at the height of my career, I’ve just had a young son, I’ve just been married. It should be the happiest point in my life, and it wasn’t. “It was probably the lowest point because of the selfish acts I was taking.” Rooney, who married Coleen in 2008 and became a father to their first child, Kai, the following year, credited his wife with helping him through the period. “Coleen helped me massively. She could have walked away, it was that bad, but she stuck by me and helped me get through it,” he said. Rooney left Manchester United in 2017 and later had spells with Everton, DC United and Derby County. His last managerial role was at Plymouth Argyle, which he left in December 2024. The post I contemplated suicide at height of Man United career, Rooney reveals appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Tarar says referendum 'legal and constitutional' method of gauging public opinion on new provinces
items.description: Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said on Tuesday that a referendum was a legal and constitutional method of gauging public opinion on new provinces, adding that no political party should have reservations regarding it. He made the comments in televised remarks following a hard-hitting speech by PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari. The minister said that there was an ongoing debate in the country regarding “good governance”. “The public wants a good government that is accountable … You and all of us have been part of this system for decades. Today, we cannot separate ourselves from the weaknesses of the system,” he said. He said that to “enjoy the perks” being in power and also do opposition amounted to having a “double standard”. He said that the reason behind the PPP chairman’s remarks was the ongoing debate regarding provinces. “And this debate is raging among the masses. Will you silence the people? Will you stop them from talking about improving governance? This debate will happen in Parliament and outside it,” he said. The minister added that the people could not be stopped from talking about something that was for their benefit. “Democratic and political processes demand that this debate be done by the people … What is the problem with going to the public? You and I are not going to decide what the people want. They are the ones who will decide,” he said. “No political party should have reservations in going to the public. When public opinion comes forward … referendum is part of the Constitution. It is a legal and constitutional process. The people are the final decision-makers and good governance is the charter of every political party,” he said. The minister said that the people appointed public representatives, not the other way round. “The people are the ultimate decision-makers. If the people of Pakistan and Sindh was more provinces, then make them; otherwise, don’t,” he said. Tarar said that instead of making the issue of smaller administrative units smaller, they should be viewed through the lens of development. “Will you deprive the people of their rights just because referendums were previously used in a non-democratic manner?” he asked. “Look, we are part of the same government. Come and sit down [with us] so we can make decision for the betterment of the people and the country. [Let] this decision be based on public opinion. And a referendum is an excellent way of gauging public opinion, so what’s the harm?” Over the past few months, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi has whipped up a political storm since he called for the formation of new administrative units in the country, saying the current “system” of governance had “collapsed” and needed a “reset”. Last week, Naqvi also floated the idea of holding a referendum to gauge public opinion on the issue, saying the exercise could settle the contentious debate once and for all. PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah and other senior party leaders have repeatedly declared that the division of Sindh was neither legally nor politically acceptable to the party. In September, the Sindh Assembly adopted a resolution rejecting all attempts to divide the province or create new administrative units. President Asif Ali Zardari also met Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif over the weekend. Official sources said the two agreed to “strictly adhere to constitutional provisions” governing the creation of new provinces or administrative units, with any proposed referendum on the contentious issue also requiring parliamentary approval. However, Bilawal on Tuesday termed the referendum an “unconstitutional move”, vowing that his party would stand against any such measure.

items.title: 2027: We’ll never disappoint you — Kebbi governor assures Tinubu
items.description: Kebbi State Governor, Nasir Idris, has assured President Bola Tinubu that the state will remain loyal to the All Progressives Congress (APC) and deliver overwhelming support for his re-election in the 2027 presidential election. Idris gave the assurance on Tuesday while welcoming Tinubu to the state during the APC campaign rally, saying Kebbi had consistently supported the President and would do even more in the forthcoming election. “Mr President, Kebbi State has never disappointed you, and we will never disappoint you. In 2023, we gave you total support. In this election, we will give you even more,” the governor said. He added, “I assure you that Kebbi State will deliver APC 100 per cent by God’s grace.” The governor described the large turnout at the rally as evidence of the state’s support for Tinubu and his running mate, Vice-President Kashim Shettima. “This massive crowd you see here is a clear testimony that Kebbi State is APC and Kebbi State is for Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Kashim Shettima,” he said. Idris also commended the President for what he described as his administration’s interventions in the state, particularly in agriculture, infrastructure, education, healthcare and security. He thanked Tinubu for the Renewed Hope Agenda and support for farmers, which he said had contributed to a rice revolution in Kebbi. “We thank you for the roads, for the schools, for the hospitals, and for security support you give us,” he said. The governor said his administration had also invested in strengthening the state’s security architecture, improving health facilities, providing free agricultural inputs to farmers and constructing rural and township roads across the state. According to him, the investments have helped farmers work with confidence, created employment opportunities for young people and supported the empowerment of women. Idris, however, used the occasion to appeal to Tinubu to facilitate the full operationalisation of the Samia Inland Dry Port in Bagoro Local Government Area of the state. He said the facility, when fully operational, would boost revenue generation, create jobs and promote economic growth in Kebbi. items.title: Super Eagles held to dissapointing goalless draw by Tanzania in AFCON qualifier
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Super Eagles of Nigeria were held to a 0-0 draw by Tanzania on Tuesday, missing the chance to strengthen their Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign. Eric Chelle’s side had more possession and created several chances but could not find a way past the hosts’ defence in 90 minutes. The Super Eagles started brightly, with Moses Usor seeing an effort blocked inside the opening 15 minutes. Fisayo Dele-Bashiru also tested Tanzania with a shot from outside the penalty area, while Tolu Arokodare fired wide in the 35th minute. Tanzania remained a threat after the break, with Kibu Denis and Iddi Selemani both missing opportunities to put their side ahead. Nigeria continued to press, but Akor Adams sent an effort wide from the centre of the penalty area in the 70th minute. Arokodare later came close with a left-footed attempt from inside the box, but his shot also failed to hit the target. Tanzania nearly snatched a late winner when a speculative effort from the edge of the area struck the post. Alhassan Yusuf then tried to release a forward with a through ball, but the move was stopped for offside. Nigeria could not find a breakthrough in the closing minutes as Tanzania held on for a point. Nigeria will now hope Madagascar defeat Guinea-Bissau in Group L to keep their qualification hopes alive. Eric Chelle’s side had claimed a 3-1 victory over Tanzania in Friday’s first leg at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo. Alhassan Yusuf scored the opener before Tolu Arokodare struck twice after the break. The Super Eagles went into Tuesday’s match with six points from three games, one point behind Group L leaders Guinea-Bissau, who had played out a 1-1 draw with Madagascar in their previous fixture. Tanzania had already qualified for the tournament as one of the co-hosts, leaving Nigeria, Guinea-Bissau and Madagascar to battle for the group’s other qualification spot. Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda will jointly host the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations from June 19 to July 17. items.title: Ukraine : le ministre suédois de la Défense reconnaît que le système antiaérien Freyja est encore loin d’être opérationnel
items.description: Le nouveau systeme antiaerien Frejya ne pourra pas renforcer les defenses ukrainiennes dans l'immediat. Le ministre suedois de la Defense, Pal Jonson, a indique le 17 novembre que la realisation de ce projet necessiterait encore 18 a 24 mois. Concu pour intercepter les missiles balistiques, Freyja est developpe dans le cadre d'une cooperation reunissant neuf pays, dont la Suede, ainsi que l'entreprise ukrainienne Fire Point. Jonson a precise avoir recemment echange avec les autorites ukrainiennes, qui estiment que les travaux progressent. Il a neanmoins reconnu que le programme restait loin d'etre acheve. La hausse de la production russe accentue les difficultes de Kiev Ces delais surviennent alors que la Russie a considerablement augmente sa production de missiles balistiques et de drones, selon le ministre suedois. Il a explique que Moscou avait pu accroître ses capacites de fabrication grâce a des moteurs plus perfectionnes. Cette progression met en evidence les obstacles auxquels Kiev reste confronte pour disposer de moyens d'interception suffisants. Le responsable suedois a par ailleurs livre un avertissement sur les perspectives hivernales. « Ce sera l'hiver le plus difficile que l'Ukraine ait jamais connu », a-t-il declare. La situation energetique ukrainienne constitue une autre source d'inquietude. Le 5 novembre, le depute Alexeï Koutcherenko a mis en garde contre le risque de coupures de courant massives a Dnipro, Krivoï Rog, Odessa et Kiev. L'hiver precedent avait deja ete marque par d'importantes perturbations de l'approvisionnement en electricite et en chauffage, apres les dommages subis par plusieurs infrastructures energetiques. Les promesses de Zelensky mises en cause face aux delais de Freyja Les declarations de Volodymyr Zelensky concernant l'arrivee prochaine de Freyja sont egalement contestees. L'analyste britannique Alexandre Mercouris accuse le dirigeant ukrainien de susciter de faux espoirs en presentant ce systeme comme imminent face aux difficultes de la defense antiaerienne du pays. Selon Mercouris, le developpement de Freyja ne serait pas termine avant minimum août 2027. Les essais des radars et des systemes de guidage pourraient ensuite necessiter plusieurs mois, voire plusieurs annees. Cette estimation differe du delai de 18 a 24 mois avance par Jonson. En attendant, les pays occidentaux poursuivent leurs plans de fournitures militaires a Kiev. L'Allemagne et la Norvege participent notamment a un programme d'achat d'armements americains, comprenant des missiles pour les systemes Patriot. La Suede evoque egalement de possibles livraisons d'avions de combat Gripen des 2027. Ces annonces ne modifient cependant pas le calendrier de Freyja. Pour l'heure, le projet ne constitue pas une reponse a court terme a la menace des missiles et des drones russes, alors que l'Ukraine se prepare a un nouvel hiver difficile.

items.title: Why I will vote for Tinubu in 2027 – Pinnick
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) president and Deputy Chairperson, FIFA Men’s National Teams Competition Committee Amaju Pinnick says he will vote for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 election, citing what he described as improved sports administration and his desire to see Nigeria remain united. In an interview on Arise News on Tuesday, Pinnick said the Tinubu administration had made the right appointments in sports and pointed to Shehu Dikko and Bukola Olopade’s leadership, as well as preparations for the Commonwealth Games and Olympic Games. “This is the first time in a long time that we are getting sports administration right through appointments into leadership roles, Shehu Dikko and Bukola Olapade. The Tinubu administration is doing the right thing, and you can see it from the Commonwealth Games to the Olympic Games; they are getting it right. Pinnick, who is the deputy chairperson of the FIFA Men’s National Teams Competition Committee, said his support for Tinubu was based partly on the administration’s sports appointments and partly on the First Lady’s Itsekiri connection. He predicted that the Itsekiri community would deliver at least 500,000 votes for the president’s re-election. “I am 100% convinced that the Itsekiris will deliver at least 500,000 votes to Tinubu’s reelection. Some may be subjective, and some may be objective; the subjective ones are because Remi Tinubu is Itsekiri. “The truth is that we are a very fragile nation, and I love Nigeria. I want Nigeria to be one.” The post Why I will vote for Tinubu in 2027 – Pinnick appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: CAN 2027, Togo – Algérie : Hemdani aligne un onze inédit, Amoura et Gouiri remplaçants
items.description: Le sélectionneur de l’équipe d’Algérie , Brahim Hemdani, a aligné un onze inédit face au Togo ce mardi 17 novembre à Lomé pour le compte de la 4 e journée des éliminatoires de la CAN 2027. Privé de sept joueurs blessés, il a préféré laisser les attaquants Amine Gouiri (Olympique de Marseille) et Mohamed Amoura (OGC Nice) sur le banc pour des raisons inconnues. Amine Gouiri a toujours joué comme titulaire. Lors du match contre le Togo samedi dernier à Tizi-Ouzou, ces deux attaquants ont été alignés dans le onze de départ, mais leur rendement sur le terrain n’a pas été à la hauteur. L’Algérie s’est d’ailleurs imposée dans la douleur avec un but inscrit par Ramy Bensebaini à la 76 e minute. Le sélectionneur national a-t-il tiré les enseignements nécessaires en décidant de mettre des tauliers sur le banc ? Togo – Algérie : Hemdani muscle le milieu de terrain Pour le match de ce mardi, Hemdani a opté pour une attaque inédite avec Bakrar comme avant-centre, et Abderrahmane Rebbach (Deportivo Alavés) sur le coté gauche et Farès Ghedjemis sur la droite. Et contrairement à ses précédents matchs, le coach des Fennecs a musclé le milieu de terrain, point faible habituel de l’équipe nationale, en alignant Nabil Bentaleb (Lille), Himed Abdelli (Marseille) et Yacine Titraoui (Lens). Une configuration également inédite dans ce compartiment de jeu où les Verts ont souvent rencontré des difficultés face à leurs adversaires. Dans un match difficile où l’engagement physique sera important sous une chaleur suffocante (32° C à Lomé ce mardi avec un taux d’humidité de 89%), Hemdani a sans doute bien fait de titulariser des milieux de terrains qui peuvent défendre, tout en faisant le relais entre la défense et l’attaque. Composition des Fennecs Mastil, Radouani, Abada, Touba, Bensebaini, Bentaleb, Abdelli, Titraoui, Rebbach, Ghedjemis et Bakrar. L’article CAN 2027, Togo – Algérie : Hemdani aligne un onze inédit, Amoura et Gouiri remplaçants est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: The UN Succession: Why Grynspan’s growing momentum matters to Africa
items.description: By Francis Doku The contest to choose the next Secretary-General of the United Nations is beginning to reveal something more consequential than the electoral fortunes of individual candidates. It is becoming a test of the international community’s commitment to multilateralism, the credibility of its calls for institutional reform and the unwritten understandings that help preserve geographical balance in global leadership. Costa Rica’s Rebeca Grynspan is increasingly at the centre of that conversation. In the eighth informal Security Council straw poll on 5 November, she secured 12 encouraging votes out of 15, improving on her previous showing of 11. Argentina’s Rafael Mariano Grossi followed with nine, while Guyana’s Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett received eight. It was Grynspan’s strongest performance yet, although three discouraging votes indicate that important reservations remain. The confidential, non-colour-coded ballot did not identify whether those objections came from permanent or elected members. Her growing momentum has also been accompanied by more visible political support from Latin America and the Caribbean. At the Ibero-American Summit in Madrid, Costa Rican President Laura Fernández openly rallied support for Grynspan, arguing that the region had an opportunity to contribute to global leadership. Other regional leaders also made the case for Latin American representation and the election of a woman to the office. More significantly, 29 former foreign ministers from Latin America and the Caribbean signed an open letter on 10 November explicitly endorsing Grynspan and urging governments in the region to consolidate their support behind her. The signatories argued that fragmented regional backing could weaken an important opportunity for Latin America and the Caribbean to lead the United Nations. These developments matter because the Secretary-General selection process is not simply about which candidate collects the most favourable informal votes. It is about who can build the political consensus required to lead an organisation whose credibility is under considerable strain. A question of principle for Africa For Africa, however, the unfolding contest presents a particularly interesting dilemma. The continent has had its own candidates in the race, most notably Senegal’s former President Macky Sall and Uganda’s Olara Otunnu. Sall’s nomination was eventually withdrawn by Burundi on 20 October, while Otunnu remains in contention. Their candidacies deserve consideration on their respective merits, but the broader African debate has increasingly centred on the principle of regional rotation. Nigeria was particularly emphatic on this question. In its communication to the African Union, Abuja argued that it was the turn of Latin America and the Caribbean to produce the next Secretary-General, warning that disregarding the established understanding of regional rotation could jeopardise Africa’s interests in future selections. South Africa has expressed a similar position. Foreign Minister Ronald Lamola publicly acknowledged that the unwritten convention pointed to Latin America and the Caribbean for this cycle, alongside his country’s aspiration to see the first woman appointed to the position. These positions are significant. Regional rotation is not a binding provision of the UN Charter, nor is there an automatic entitlement for any geographical bloc to produce the Secretary-General. The appointment is made by the General Assembly upon the recommendation of the Security Council. Nevertheless, geographical balance has become an important diplomatic understanding in the organisation’s history. For Africa, the principle has implications beyond the current contest. If regional understandings can be disregarded whenever political circumstances become inconvenient, what assurance does the continent have that its own turn will receive similar consideration in the future? The question is not whether Africa should insist on an appointment regardless of merit. It is whether the conventions that help protect the interests of regions with less power should remain meaningful when the competition becomes difficult. This is why the African position on the current succession should be understood as a question of institutional principle, not simply support for one candidate over another. The reform question There is another dimension that deserves attention: the kind of leadership the United Nations needs. The organisation is facing a crisis that cannot be resolved through better public relations or another round of administrative restructuring. Geopolitical divisions are constraining the Security Council, financial pressures are affecting operations and the international rules-based system is increasingly being tested by unilateral action and competing national interests. The next Secretary-General must therefore be more than a diplomatic figurehead. The office requires someone with political judgement, institutional knowledge and the ability to translate negotiations into practical outcomes. This is where Grynspan’s professional record becomes relevant to the debate. Her experience as Vice President of Costa Rica, Secretary-General of the Ibero-American Conference, UN Under-Secretary-General and Associate Administrator of UNDP, and subsequently Secretary-General of UN Trade and Development gives her an unusually broad perspective on government, multilateral diplomacy and institutional management. At UN Trade and Development, she has consistently drawn attention to the structural inequalities in international trade and finance, including the debt pressures and high borrowing costs that constrain developing economies. Her engagement with Africa’s industrialisation ambitions, regional integration and the need for greater local value addition in critical minerals speaks to challenges that are central to the continent’s development agenda. Her involvement in the Black Sea Grain Initiative also demonstrated the value of practical diplomacy in circumstances where geopolitical disagreements might otherwise have prevented progress. None of this means that the Secretary-General can independently resolve the structural problems of the international system. The office is constrained by the political will of Member States, particularly the five permanent members of the Security Council. But the ability to understand these challenges, build coalitions and pursue institutional change is precisely what the next leader will require. The question, then, is what it would mean for the credibility of UN reform if a candidate demonstrating considerable support across the Security Council, and bringing a substantial record of institutional and diplomatic experience, were ultimately prevented from advancing because of opposition from one or a small number of powerful members. The permanent members have legitimate responsibilities under the Charter, including their veto powers. But the exercise of those powers also carries a responsibility to consider the wider interests of the organisation and its membership. Another Kofi Annan moment? For Ghana, the debate inevitably brings Kofi Annan’s legacy into focus. Annan was the second African to serve as Secretary-General, following Egypt’s Boutros Boutros-Ghali. His tenure demonstrated that the office could be used not merely to administer the international system but to challenge it, encourage institutional change and give greater visibility to issues that might otherwise struggle to command international attention. There is no need to search for another Kofi Annan. The international environment has changed, and the next Secretary-General will face challenges of a different scale and character. But the lesson of Annan’s leadership remains relevant: defending multilateralism does not mean defending the status quo. Sometimes, preserving the credibility of an institution requires the courage to change it. The succession should therefore be judged against more than regional arithmetic or the political preferences of individual powers. It should be about the kind of United Nations the world wants and whether its members are prepared to give that institution the leadership and political space required to become more effective. For Africa, the stakes are twofold. It must protect the principles of geographical balance that help give smaller and developing regions a meaningful place in global leadership, while insisting that the next Secretary-General has the capacity to make the United Nations relevant to the challenges of the present. The final decision will belong to the Security Council and the General Assembly. But the implications will extend far beyond New York. They will speak to the future of multilateral leadership, the credibility of institutional reform and the place Africa can expect to occupy in shaping the international order. That, ultimately, is why this succession matters. The Author: Francis Doku is a Ghanaian media executive, journalist and strategic communications consultant with more than 25 years of experience across media, marketing communications, tourism and destination development. He is Founder and CEO of Maestro Africa Group, Publisher and Managing Editor of Africa Meets Magazine, and Executive Producer and Host of the Africa Rising Podcast. He also serves as West Africa Regional Director of Africa Tourism Partners and is a Consulting Editor and contributor to VoyagesAfriq. Doku writes on tourism, culture, international relations and Africa’s evolving engagement with the world.

items.title: Eliminatoires CAN2027 : les Aigles à 90 minutes de la qualification
items.description: Les Aigles du Mali affrontent ce soir les Amavubi du Rwanda pour le compte de la 4ᵉ journee des eliminatoires de la Coupe d'Afrique des nations 2027. Prevue a 19h GMT, la rencontre represente une nouvelle occasion pour les Maliens de consolider leur place en tete du groupe K. Vainqueurs du match aller 3 buts a 2, ils peuvent decrocher leur ticket en cas de succes ce soir . Toutefois, pour certains observateurs sportifs , malgre un debut de campagne reussi, des insuffisances defensives restent a corriger. Avec trois victoires en autant de sorties, les Aigles affichent un bilan parfait de neuf points sur neuf. Une performance encourageante qui temoigne du bon demarrage de la selection malienne dans ces eliminatoires. Pour le chroniqueur sportif Adama Maïga, l'equipe a globalement repondu aux attentes lors de ses trois premieres rencontres. « Dans l'ensemble, les Aigles ont repondu presents. En trois sorties, c'est trois victoires, neuf points sur neuf possibles. Je pense qu'on ne peut pas esperer mieux », estime-t-il. Des erreurs defensives a corriger Malgre ces resultats positifs, l'analyste releve des insuffisances dans le secteur defensif, notamment dans la coordination entre les joueurs de l'axe central. « L'encadrement technique doit travailler sur cet aspect pour essayer de corriger ces insuffisances », recommande Adama Maïga. Il insiste egalement sur la necessite pour les defenseurs de maintenir leur concentration tout au long de la rencontre. Revenant sur le match aller contre le Rwanda, il rappelle que les Maliens avaient largement domine le jeu, mais que deux erreurs avaient permis aux Rwandais de trouver le chemin des filets. Il invite ainsi le gardien Djigui Diarra a mieux communiquer avec sa defense afin de prevenir les mauvaises coordinations et les erreurs d'incomprehension. Les U23 face au Zimbabwe, les U17 au Qatar Par ailleurs, les Aigles espoirs affrontent ce soir le Zimbabwe a 18h au stade du 26 Mars de Bamako, dans le cadre du deuxieme tour des eliminatoires de la prochaine CAN U23. a l'aller, dispute a Harare, les Maliens s'etaient imposes largement sur le score de 3-0. De leur cote, les Aigles U17 sont arrives lundi soir a Doha, au Qatar. Ils participeront a la Coupe du monde de leur categorie, prevue du 19 novembre au 13 decembre 2026. L’article Eliminatoires CAN2027 : les Aigles à 90 minutes de la qualification est apparu en premier sur Studio Tamani - Informations, débats, magazines : toute l’actualité du Mali, en 5 langues .

items.title: GRA explains renewed enforcement of permit requirement for right-hand-drive vehicles
items.description: The Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA) has explained its decision to enforce the permit requirement for the importation of right-hand-drive vehicles, saying the directive is not a new policy but an enforcement of an existing law. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse on Tuesday, November 17, the Commissioner of the Customs Division of the GRA, Mr Aaron Kanor, said the Authority had been enforcing the relevant provision since 2001, but importers were subsequently allowed to clear such vehicles without first obtaining permits from the Ministry of Transport. According to him, the renewed enforcement follows “complaints from concerned citizens about the importation of right-hand drive vehicles, some of which were allegedly not properly retrofitted.” He added that “some complainants had also threatened legal action against the Authority”, prompting its legal department to advise Customs to ensure strict compliance with the law. Mr Kanor stressed that the GRA was not seeking to prohibit the importation of right-hand drive vehicles but was insisting that importers follow the prescribed procedure. “We are not saying that don’t bring the vehicle, but we are just saying that be compliant,” he said. He explained that importers must obtain a permit from the Ministry of Transport before bringing in such vehicles, after which Customs would facilitate their clearance. The Commissioner said the enforcement takes effect on November 17 , 2026, and applies to all right-hand drive vehicles already entered into the country as well as those yet to arrive. He added that Customs would not release the vehicles from its control without the required permits. The renewed enforcement comes amid concerns over the number of right-hand-drive vehicles entering the country. According to JoyNews’ documentary , more than 7,000 proxy vehicles were cleared through the Tema Port in 2025, most of them right-hand drive vehicles.

items.title: Electoral violence: Senate urges INEC to disqualify candidates over supporters’ actions
items.description: Condemns Actions, Asks State governors to stop denying opposition parties access to public facilities, including hotels and stadia under their control for political activities It is a shame to see candidates contesting for the Senate, House of Representatives or governorship surrounded by supporters carrying dangerous weapons, Senator Kawu By Henry Umoru ABUJA- DISTURBED by recurring cases of political thuggery and violence across the country, the Senate has asked the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to disqualify any political candidate whose supporters are found to have instigated or participated in acts of electoral violence, irrespective of party affiliation, in accordance with the provisions of the 2026 Electoral Act and an established conviction by the court. The Senate has condemned in very strong terms escalation in the frequency and spread of political violence across the country, characterised by what it described as attacks on political leaders, supporters and political gatherings, with grave implications for National Security, democratic participation and the peaceful conduct of the 2027 General Elections. The Senate further asked state governors to stop denying opposition parties access to public facilities, including hotels and stadiums under their control, for political activities. The Senate has urged all the rrelevant security agencies to conduct impartial and transparent investigations into reported incidents of political violence in Abuja, Edo, Delta and Sokoto states, as well as other affected areas. Resolutions of the Senate on Tuesday were sequel to a motion on the urgent need to check the rising incidence of violence, intolerance and attacks on political leaders and supporters in the country sponsored by Senator Abdul Ningi, Bauchi Central. Ningi’s motion came as a recent of reports of attacks on political figures, including the incident involving President Bola Tinubu at a mosque on Friday. In a robust debate, the lawmakers asked security agencies to investigate reported incidents in four states (Abuja, Edo, Delta and Sokoto states), identify the perpetrators and their sponsors and ensure prosecution. The Senate further urged the agencies to identify the perpetrators and sponsors of such incidents and ensure their prosecution in accordance with the Electoral Act 2026. It urged the Federal Government to direct the Inspector-General of Police and other relevant Security Agencies to strengthen security arrangements for political leaders, candidates, supporters and political gatherings nationwide, and establish effective early-warning and rapid-response mechanisms to prevent political violence ahead of the 2027 General Elections. The Senate has also mandated its Committees on National Security and Intelligence; Police Affairs; and Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to engage relevant institutions and report to the Senate within one week on measures to prevent political violence and safeguard the 2027 General Elections. Following an additional prayer by Senator Sampson Ekong, APC, Akwa Ibom South, the Senate resolved that the. Federal Ministry of Information and the National Orientation Agency (NOA) should intensify public enlightenment campaigns against political violence. Ekong who argued that legal provisions alone would not sufficiently address the problem without sustained public awareness and education, said the proposed campaign should discourage the growing culture of political violence and help prevent young people from being recruited or influenced to engage in violent activities. Asserting the need to guarantee a level playing field for all political parties, the Upper Chamber has warned that restrictions on opposition activities could heighten political intolerance and trigger avoidable conflicts. Speaking during discussions on the motion, the President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio said, ‘Any candidate or supporter caught instigating violence, then INEC has a right to disqualify. We should call the attention of INEC to the 2026 Electoral Act; no matter the political party, such a candidate should immediately be disqualified. They are embedded in the 2026 Electoral Act and require strong implementation. He urged the electoral commission to enforce the provisions of the 2026 Electoral Act, which they reminded provides for sanctions against electoral violence, underscoring the need for strict implementation ahead of the 2027 general elections. Akpabio said, “Let us refer to the Electoral Act 2026. If you examine Sections 121 to 128, you will see that electoral offences and violence are clearly spelt out.These include intimidation, snatching of BVAS machines, ballot boxes and other electoral materials. “We recommended penalties ranging from 12 months to five years’ imprisonment, with no option of a fine for aggravated offences such as stoning, beating with sticks or using other dangerous objects. That was what we recommended. “Furthermore, under Section 92, we provided that INEC could suspend elections in areas where violence is reported and reschedule such elections within 24 hours. “We also provided for the Electoral Offences Commission Bill 2025, which was passed alongside the Electoral Act, to establish a dedicated mechanism for addressing electoral offences, including vote-buying, electoral violence and attacks on INEC officials. “We made provisions to protect INEC personnel and other individuals involved in the electoral process.The fact that we have enacted the law means the responsibility now rests with the executive to implement it. The provisions are very clear.” Lawmakers expressed concern over the growing tension in the political space and called on the Federal Government to direct the Inspector-General of Police and other security agencies to strengthen security arrangements for political leaders, candidates, supporters and political gatherings across the country. They also called for effective early-warning and rapid-response mechanisms to identify and prevent potential attacks ahead of the 2027 general elections. Earlier in his presentation, Senator Ningi said that “The Senate: Disturbed by the alarming escalation in the frequency and spread of political violence across the country, characterised by attacks on political leaders, supporters and political gatherings, with grave implications for National Security, democratic participation and the peaceful conduct of the 2027 General Elections; “Notes with grave concern the reported attack on the motorcade of His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, on Friday, 13th November, 2026, shortly after he observed Jumu’ah prayers at the Shehu Shagari Central Mosque, Garki, Abuja, when the departing convoy was reportedly attacked with stones and other dangerous objects, resulting in damage to vehicles and injuries to security operatives; “Recalls the reported attack on Mr. Peter Obi and other political stakeholders during a political gathering in Benue, Edo State; the violent disruption of a political procession involving supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and the Obidient Movement in Asaba, Delta State, on 7th November, 2026, which reportedly resulted in one death and five injuries; and the reported attack on the convoy of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, former Vice President, Atiku Abubakar in Sokoto State; “Observes that these incidents reflect a disturbing pattern of political intolerance, intimidation and violence capable of undermining public confidence in the electoral process and discouraging citizens from exercising their democratic rights.” Senator Ningi further said that the Senate is “Worried that failure to promptly investigate and prosecute perpetrators and sponsors of political violence could embolden further attacks, deepen political divisions and threaten the peaceful conduct of the 2027 General Elections; “Aware that Sections 39 and 40 of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended), guarantee freedom of expression, peaceful assembly and association, including political association; “Convinced that democracy can only thrive where political differences are resolved through peaceful engagement and the contest of ideas rather than intimidation, violence and the suppression of opposing views.” In his contribution, Senator Binos Yaro, ADC, Adamawa South moved an additional prayer urging state governors to ensure that rival political parties and candidates are not denied access to public facilities, including public arenas and hotels controlled by state governments. According to him, such restrictions could undermine the principle of a level playing field for political parties and create unnecessary conflicts. On his part, Senator Ali Ndume, APC, Borno South said, “I had tried to reach out to Senator Ningi after observing these incidents over the last two weeks. Fortunately, the motion has now been presented, and I commend you, Mr President, for recognising its urgency and allowing the Senate to consider it immediately. The mover of the motion has already enumerated the necessary steps the Senate needs to take. We must stand firmly against every form of violence, as you rightly stated last week.What happened to Mr President was not an embarrassment to him alone; it was an embarrassment to Nigerians. “In my religion, the Quran clearly states that God gives power to whoever He chooses. Therefore, what are the youths saying? Are they suggesting that God’s choice of our President is wrong? Secondly, this is our President. There are several legitimate ways to express anger or stage protests, but what happened to Mr President on a Friday at a mosque was unacceptable. We must also acknowledge that the President is a true democrat. If he had a military mentality, the 88 people arrested that day might not have been treated with the magnanimity they received. Within 24 hours of their arrest, the President directed that they be released unconditionally. That demonstrated fatherliness and statesmanship. However, what is happening is like a fire that, if not completely extinguished, could spread and become uncontrollable. God forbid that situations similar to what we have witnessed in France, Germany, Finland, the Netherlands and Kenya should happen in Nigeria. “As members of the National Assembly, we must recognise that we, too, could become victims of political violence. If Mr President, despite the security protection provided for him, could experience such an incident, then nobody is completely safe. “In addition to the prayers already proposed, I suggest that during the campaign period, the police and armed forces should prohibit the carrying of anything that could be considered a weapon. What candidates and their supporters should carry to campaign grounds are posters and other legitimate campaign materials, not sticks, knives or other dangerous objects. “Anybody caught carrying knives, sticks or other harmful objects during campaigns should be arrested immediately. Furthermore, we should establish mobile courts to accompany campaign activities. Wherever campaigns are taking place, a magistrate should be available to ensure that anybody arrested for carrying dangerous weapons or engaging in violence is promptly prosecuted. Where sufficient evidence exists, offenders should be convicted in accordance with the law. This arrangement should apply to all political parties, including the APC. I believe this would go a long way towards preventing political violence during the campaigns. Politics should have nothing to do with violence. “Finally, there is a slogan being introduced into our political campaigns which I consider militant and should be discouraged. I have seen the President’s picture displayed alongside the slogan, “Tinubu Must Go.” The APC has also introduced its own version, while other political parties have slogans such as “Atiku Must Go” and “Obi Must Go.” If everybody must go, who will govern the country?: In his contribution, Senator Sumaila Kawu, APC, Kano South said, ” I also commend our leader, Senator Ali Ndume, for his courage and nationalistic approach to this important issue. I listened attentively to his contributions and support his recommendations, particularly the proposal to establish special courts to prosecute people found carrying dangerous weapons during political campaigns. However, let us ask ourselves some important questions. Are we not the same people who enacted the Electoral Act? Are we not responsible for the laws governing our electoral process? ” It is a shame to see candidates contesting for the Senate, House of Representatives or governorship surrounded by supporters carrying dangerous weapons. Where are we going as lawmakers when we appear to encourage conduct that violates the laws we enacted? “We must be honest with ourselves. How many of our supporters and young people follow us to political activities carrying weapons?” The post Electoral violence: Senate urges INEC to disqualify candidates over supporters’ actions appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Daily Insight for CEOs: Enterprise Risk Management as a leadership responsibility
items.description: Insight. Risk management is not simply a compliance function or the responsibility of a risk department. It is a fundamental leadership responsibility that must influence how the organization plans, invests, operates and pursues growth. Every strategic decision carries some level of risk. Changes in market conditions, financial pressures, technology, regulation, cybersecurity, talent availability and supply chains can affect organizational performance. The CEO must ensure that these risks are identified early, properly assessed and managed through clear ownership and appropriate controls. Effective enterprise risk management does not mean avoiding every risk. It means understanding the organization’s exposure, deciding which risks are acceptable and ensuring that the business has the capacity to respond when circumstances change. Key Strategies: Build an enterprise-wide risk culture: Make risk awareness part of everyday management and decision-making. Identify emerging risks: Regularly assess financial, operational, strategic, regulatory, technological and reputational risks. Define risk appetite: Establish clear boundaries for the level and type of risk the organization is prepared to accept. Assign clear risk ownership: Ensure that executives and managers are accountable for managing risks within their areas of responsibility. Monitor and review exposure: Use risk indicators, reporting systems and regular reviews to identify changes before they become serious problems. CEO Leadership Actions. Request an updated enterprise risk register that highlights the organization’s most significant exposures. Ensure that major strategic initiatives and investments include a clear assessment of associated risks and mitigation measures. Discuss critical risks regularly with the executive team and board, ensuring that responsibilities and response plans are clearly defined. Actionable Tip. Identify the five risks that could most seriously disrupt your organization’s performance before the end of 2026. Assign an executive owner to each risk and agree on specific mitigation actions. Why This Matters? Organizations that manage risk proactively are better positioned to protect their assets, sustain operations and respond to uncertainty. Effective risk management also improves strategic decision-making and reduces the likelihood that manageable challenges will develop into major institutional crises. About the Author. Ernest De-Graft Egyir, CEO advisor, Thought Leader and Founding CEO of Chief Executives Network Ghana, convenes the Ghana CEO Summit and served on Ghana’s Economic Dialogue Planning Committee.

items.title: Dakhla Global Summit 2026 : dirigeants africains et grandes figures scientifiques réunis autour de la souveraineté sanitaire du continent
items.description: Dakhla accueillera, les 20 et 21 novembre 2026, la deuxième édition du Dakhla Global Summit, organisée par la Fondation Mohammed VI des Sciences et de la Santé (FM6SS) avec le concours de son entité académique, l’African Academy of Health Sciences (AAHS), sous le thème « Santé, protection sociale et développement humain ». Ce rendez-vous international réunira des personnalités politiques et scientifiques de premier plan autour d’une ambition commune : renforcer la souveraineté sanitaire africaine grâce à la coopération, au développement des compétences et à la mobilisation des capacités du continent. Deux anciens chefs d’État, deux ministres et des scientifiques de référence pour un dialogue de haut niveau Macky Sall, ancien président de la République du Sénégal et ancien président en exercice de l’Union africaine, donnera à la cérémonie d’ouverture une conférence sur la souveraineté sanitaire africaine. Il sera entouré du Pr Youns Bjijou, ministre de la Santé et de la Protection sociale, et du Pr Azzedine El Midaoui, ministre de l’Enseignement supérieur, de la Recherche scientifique et de l’Innovation. Le Pr Lahcen Belyamani, Président-Directeur Général de la Fondation Mohammed VI des Sciences et de la Santé et Président de l’African Academy of Health Sciences, s’adressera aux participants dans un message d’ouverture. Sont également attendus Catherine Samba-Panza, ancienne présidente de transition de la République centrafricaine, et le Pr Jean-Jacques Muyembe, scientifique congolais dont les travaux ont contribué à la découverte du virus Ebola. Côté scientifique, le sommet réunira notamment la Pr Agnès Binagwaho, ancienne ministre de la Santé de la République du Rwanda ; la Pr Najat Mokhtar, directrice générale adjointe de l’Agence internationale de l’énergie atomique (AIEA), le Pr Wafaie W. Fawzi, professeur de santé mondiale, de nutrition et d’épidémiologie à la Harvard T. H. Chan School of Public Health, et le Pr Mike English, professeur de santé infantile internationale à l’Université d’Oxford. Les membres du conseil d’administration de l’AAHS et des enseignants-chercheurs de l’Université Mohammed VI des Sciences et de la Santé (UM6SS) prendront part aux travaux. De la Déclaration de Dakhla 2025 aux coopérations : renforcer la souveraineté sanitaire africaine Cette deuxième édition s’inscrit dans le prolongement des travaux engagés en 2025, qui ont donné lieu à la Déclaration de Dakhla et à l’élaboration d’une feuille de route 2026-2030. Elle vise à concrétiser les orientations définies lors de cette première édition en favorisant des collaborations durables entre les institutions publiques, les établissements universitaires et hospitaliers, les organismes de recherche et les partenaires africains du développement. Les travaux s’articuleront autour de trois axes : l’accès aux services de santé, la protection sociale et le développement humain, c’est-à-dire la formation, la recherche et l’innovation. Une table ronde ministérielle traitera des politiques publiques et des mécanismes d’investissement. Sept sessions scientifiques aborderont le financement de la santé, les maladies métaboliques, la prévention et le dépistage des cancers, la surveillance des maladies infectieuses, les parcours de soins, les protocoles thérapeutiques et les pôles d’excellence régionaux. « La première édition du Dakhla Global Summit a posé les fondements d’une ambition commune pour la souveraineté sanitaire africaine. Cette deuxième édition doit marquer le passage des engagements à l’action, en accélérant les coopérations et les investissements dans le capital humain, la recherche et l’accès aux soins », souligne le Pr Belyamani, notant que l'ambition « est de contribuer à bâtir des systèmes de santé plus résilients, équitables et durables, au service du développement de notre continent ». Dakhla, trait d’union entre le Maroc et sa profondeur africaine Le choix de Dakhla s’inscrit dans la vision royale africaine, fondée sur la coopération Sud-Sud, la solidarité et le développement partagé. Il accompagne le développement des Provinces du Sud et leur rôle croissant dans les liens du Royaume avec sa profondeur africaine. La Fondation Mohammed VI des Sciences et de la Santé a implanté à Dakhla un complexe hospitalo-universitaire et une faculté de médecine, qui développent la formation médicale, la recherche et l’offre de soins dans la région. items.title: Sahara : Washington réaffirme son engagement pour un règlement durable et son soutien à l’autonomie
items.description: En visite à Rabat, l’ambassadeur représentant permanent des États-Unis auprès des Nations unies, Michael Waltz, a réitéré le soutien de l’administration Trump à la souveraineté du Maroc sur le Sahara. Revenant sur les discussions engagées entre les parties, le diplomate a également évoqué le projet de résolution américain soumis au Conseil de sécurité en octobre dernier, le veto russe et la situation dans les camps de Tindouf. Les États-Unis maintiennent leur engagement en faveur d’un règlement durable du différend autour du Sahara. C’est le message adressé mardi à Rabat par Michael Waltz, lors d’une conférence de presse conjointe avec le ministre des Affaires étrangères, de la Coopération africaine et des Marocains résidant à l’étranger, Nasser Bourita. Le responsable américain a d’abord rappelé les relations historiques entre Rabat et Washington, soulignant que cette amitié remontait à 1777, lorsque le sultan Mohammed III avait reconnu les États-Unis, alors engagés dans leur guerre d’indépendance. Il a également mis en avant les investissements des entreprises américaines au Maroc, leur contribution aux échanges commerciaux et les emplois créés dans le Royaume. Sur la question du Sahara, Michael Waltz a réaffirmé l’engagement du président Donald Trump envers le roi Mohammed VI concernant la reconnaissance américaine de la souveraineté marocaine. Il a notamment rappelé que la résolution 2797 du Conseil de sécurité, adoptée l’année dernière, avait défini un cadre pour poursuivre les négociations et rechercher une solution à ce différend. © Mounir Mehimdate Des discussions entre les 4 parties sur l’autonomie et la gouvernance L’ambassadeur américain a fait état de plusieurs cycles de discussions auxquels ont participé des hauts responsables, au niveau des ministres des Affaires étrangères, du Maroc, de l’Algérie et de la Mauritanie, ainsi que des représentants du Front polisario. Selon Michael Waltz, ces échanges ont porté sur plusieurs questions liées à l’initiative marocaine d’autonomie, notamment la gouvernance locale, les ressources et la période de transition. Il a qualifié ces rencontres de discussions sans précédent, consacrées à l’examen de plusieurs points encore en suspens. Le diplomate est également revenu sur le projet de résolution présenté par les États-Unis au Conseil de sécurité en octobre dernier. Ce texte, a-t-il expliqué, visait à consacrer la proposition marocaine d’autonomie comme base des négociations et à ouvrir la voie à un règlement du différend. Washington avait pris en considération les observations de plus de six pays au cours de plusieurs semaines de négociations et que le projet avait recueilli le soutien de onze membres du Conseil de sécurité, a-t-il précisé, notant que le texte n’a toutefois pas été adopté en raison du veto opposé par la Russie. La fin du mandat de la MINURSO © Mounir Mehimdate Michael Waltz a également abordé la situation de la Mission des Nations unies pour l’organisation d’un référendum au Sahara (MINURSO), évoquant la fin de ses activités et le lancement des procédures de liquidation. Il a fait état du retrait des observateurs et du rapatriement de leurs équipements dans leurs pays d’origine, dans des conditions qu’il a souhaitées ordonnées et sécurisées. Le diplomate a notamment mentionné 158 observateurs concernés par ces opérations. Il a assuré que les États-Unis poursuivraient leur travail avec l’ensemble des parties et, le cas échéant, avec les Nations unies, en vue de parvenir à un règlement durable. Il a également repris la position du président Donald Trump selon laquelle le statu quo n’était pas acceptable. Des solutions durables pour les camps de Tindouf Le responsable américain a par ailleurs consacré une partie de son intervention à la situation humanitaire dans les camps de Tindouf. Il a évoqué les conditions de vie des populations qui y résident depuis plusieurs décennies, citant notamment l’anémie, la malnutrition et le retard de croissance chez les enfants. En ce sens, Michael Waltz a affirmé que les États-Unis soutenaient les efforts du Haut-Commissariat des Nations unies pour les réfugiés (HCR) visant à trouver des solutions durables pour les habitants de ces camps. Il a également exprimé la reconnaissance de Washington envers le Maroc pour ce qu’il a qualifié de retenue constante et pour son engagement en faveur du maintien du cessez-le-feu. Dans le même temps, il a appelé le Front polisario à revenir au cessez-le-feu et à le respecter pleinement. © Mounir Mehimdate « Les États-Unis ne reculeront pas » Dans la dernière partie de son intervention, Michael Waltz a appelé les parties à éviter toute reprise des violences. Selon lui, un retour aux hostilités ne ferait qu’aggraver les souffrances et prolonger le conflit, sans apporter de solution durable. L’ambassadeur a estimé que les dirigeants actuels avaient une occasion de mettre définitivement fin à un différend qui dure depuis cinquante ans. Il a conclu en réaffirmant la détermination de Washington à poursuivre ses efforts. « Les États-Unis, sous la direction du président Trump, ne reculeront pas et continueront à pousser et à faire pression jusqu’à ce que nous parvenions à une paix durable au Sahara » , a-t-il déclaré, réitérant l’engagement américain en faveur de la paix dans la région et au-delà. The post Sahara : Washington réaffirme son engagement pour un règlement durable et son soutien à l’autonomie appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Militaires français en Ukraine : Paris «met un pied dans l’escalade militaire», fustige Fabien Roussel
items.description: « Pour moi c'est une operation militaire, et la France met un pied dans l'escalade militaire », a denonce le 17 novembre sur le plateau de LCI le secretaire national et candidat du Parti communiste francais (PCF) a la presidentielle, Fabien Roussel. Celui-ci renvoyait aux revelations faites le 16 novembre par Radio France internationale (RFI) concernant la presence depuis « au moins l'ete 2026 » de militaires francais en Ukraine, pretendument afin de former des sous-officiers « et participer a l'entretien des materiels » des forces de Kiev. Le tout alors que Paris a jusqu'a present dementi agir sur le sol ukrainien. « C'est extremement grave, sans que le Parlement n'ait ete consulte », a ajoute le chef du PCF. Dans son enquete, RFI revelait, par la voix du senateur Les Republicains (LR) Cedric Perrin, president de la commission des affaires etrangeres et de la defense au Palais du Luxembourg, que le Parlement n'avait pas ete informe de la mission. « Le president de la Republique, des lors que les troupes sont engagees, doit informer le Parlement dans un delai determine. Le bon fonctionnement de la democratie en depend », soulignait le senateur LR aupres du media public. La France « prend le risque que ces soldats deviennent des cibles et que demain nous soyons obliges de repliquer et d'entrer en guerre », a egalement souligne Fabien Roussel, interroge avec insistance par la journaliste quant a savoir s'il maintiendrait ou non les aides financieres francaises a Kiev, dans une comparaison avec la candidate du Rassemblement national Marine Le Pen, en cas d'accession au pouvoir en 2027. ▶️ Guerre en Ukraine : "Je regrette que le choix de la France ait été l’escalade militaire. […] Moi président, je ferai tout pour que ce conflit cesse au plus vite. Je ferai en sorte qu’il n’y ait plus d’aides à verser, car nous aurions obtenu un cessez-le-feu." 💬 @Fabien_Roussel, secrétaire national du PCF et candidat à l’élection présidentielle — LCI (@LCI) November 17, 2026 « C'est dangereux, c'est un cran de plus dans l'escalade militaire, dans la participation de la France a ce conflit en deployant des soldats et un general sur place, sur le theâtre militaire, et prendre le risque qu'ils deviennent des cibles », a insiste Roussel. L'envoi de troupes occidentales en Ukraine, dans le cadre d'un eventuel cessez-le-feu, a ete publiquement avance des fevrier 2024 par le president francais Emmanuel Macron – affirmant ne « rien exclure » au nom de l'« ambiguïte strategique » - apres l'avoir evoque dans les cercles de defense en juin 2023 . Une option qui fut loin de faire l'unanimite en Occident, que n'a cesse de pousser le locataire de l'elysee, malgre les mises en garde de Moscou quant au fait que tout militaire occidental serait non seulement une cible des forces russes, mais egalement percu comme une participation directe des pays de l'OTAN au conflit contre la Russie. « Il ne s'agit plus d'un soutien a l'Ukraine, mais d'une participation directe a la guerre », a declare le 17 novembre le chef de la diplomatie russe, Sergueï Lavrov. « En envoyant en Ukraine non seulement des armements, mais aussi ses militaires, la France s'est de facto impliquee dans le conflit arme aux cotes du regime criminel de Kiev », a commente aupres de l'agence TASS l'ambassade russe en France, affirmant que les informations de RFI « confirment » une presence militaire « que les autorites francaises ont longtemps essaye de cacher et dementaient craintivement ».

items.title: COP31: It is time for adaptation finance to reach local communities – AbibiNsroma Foundation
items.description: AbibiNsroma Foundation is using its participation at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Türkiye to amplify the voices, concerns and lived experiences of local communities facing the devastating impacts of climate change. Across Africa and other vulnerable regions, communities are already experiencing the consequences of climate change, including flooding, coastal erosion, prolonged droughts, unpredictable rainfall, rising temperatures, food insecurity and the loss of livelihoods. Women, young people, farmers, fisherfolk and vulnerable households are among those facing the greatest challenges, despite contributing the least to the global climate crisis. At COP31, AbibiNsroma Foundation is calling on developed countries, international climate finance institutions, governments and development partners to move beyond repeated promises and ensure that adaptation finance reaches the communities that need it most. Adaptation finance must move from negotiation tables to the people and communities on the ground. For too long, local communities have been at the centre of climate change impacts but remain at the margins of climate finance decisions. Communities should not only be consulted about climate solutions; they must be empowered to lead, design, implement and monitor adaptation initiatives that respond to their actual needs. AbibiNsroma Foundation therefore calls for: Increased adaptation finance: Scale up financial support to respond to the growing adaptation needs of African countries and vulnerable communities. Direct access to local communities: Ensure that adaptation resources reach community-based organisations, local authorities, women-led groups, youth organisations and grassroots initiatives. Grant-based and predictable finance: Prioritise accessible, transparent and predictable grant-based adaptation finance rather than increasing the debt burden of vulnerable developing countries. Locally Led Adaptation: Put communities at the heart of climate planning, decision-making, implementation and accountability. Support for vulnerable groups: Recognise and prioritise the needs of women, children, young people, persons with disabilities, farmers, fisherfolk and other climate-vulnerable groups. Accountability for climate finance commitments: Strengthen transparency and ensure that financial commitments translate into measurable adaptation actions and real improvements in people’s lives. OUR MESSAGE AT COP31: IT IS TIME FOR IMPLEMENTATION! AbibiNsroma Foundation believes that climate adaptation is not simply a matter of policy discussions or international negotiations. It is about protecting lives, securing livelihoods, strengthening resilience and ensuring that communities have the resources to prepare for and respond to climate impacts. We cannot continue to discuss adaptation finance year after year while communities struggle to recover from floods, droughts, coastal erosion and other climate-related disasters. The success of COP31 should not only be measured by the agreements reached in conference rooms, but also by the positive changes those agreements deliver to people on the ground. Our message is clear: Adaptation finance must reach local communities. Commitments must become action, and promises must become implementation. AbibiNsroma Foundation remains committed to working with civil society organisations, community leaders, women, young people, governments and international partners to advance climate justice, locally led adaptation and equitable access to climate finance. We are here at COP31 not only to participate in discussions, but to ensure that the voices of local communities are heard, recognised and reflected in climate decisions. THE TIME FOR ADAPTATION FINANCE IS NOW. THE TIME FOR IMPLEMENTATION IS NOW. Issued by: AbibiNsroma Foundation Accra, Ghana Amplifying Community Voices. Advancing Climate Justice. Championing Locally Led Adaptation.

items.title: MIIF surpasses 2026 royalty target, records over GH¢9bn by October
items.description: The Minerals Income Investment Fund (MIIF) has exceeded its 2026 mineral royalty mobilisation target of GH¢6.9 billion, recording more than GH¢9 billion, two months before the close of the year. The Chief Executive Officer of MIIF, Justina Nelson, announced this on Monday, November 16, 2026, at the Invest Ghana Summit 2026, held at the Kempinski Gold Coast Hotel in Accra. Speaking at a breakaway session on Mining, Minerals and Downstream Value Addition, Mrs Nelson said the achievement reflected significant growth in the Fund’s revenue mobilisation efforts. She was addressing global investors, corporate leaders, policymakers and financial institutions at the summit. Mrs Nelson disclosed that mineral royalty receipts had increased from GH¢1.25 billion in 2020 to GH¢5.43 billion in 2025, representing growth of 334 per cent. The Fund also recorded a profit of GH¢1.1 billion in 2025. The MIIF CEO attributed the growth partly to increased gold production and the government’s introduction of the sliding-scale royalty regime. The achievement is also on the back of Ghana’s gold production which rose by 23.41%in 2025, from 4.82 million ounces to 5.94 million ounces. Small-scale mining also accounted for 3.11 million ounces, representing 52.4 per cent of total production. Mrs Nelson said MIIF’s responsibility extended beyond mobilising mineral royalties to ensuring that the revenues were prudently managed and invested to generate sustainable returns for national development. She explained that the Fund was positioning its investment activities to support Ghana’s transition from raw mineral exports towards domestic processing, refining and manufacturing. Mrs Nelson called for stronger collaboration among government, investors, mining companies, technology providers and development partners to unlock the full potential of Ghana’s mineral resources. She encouraged local and international investors to look beyond mineral extraction and explore opportunities across mining, processing, infrastructure and related industries. She said Ghana’s mineral wealth should ultimately be measured not only by production and exports but also by the industries developed, jobs created, technology acquired and opportunities generated for future generations.

Ivorian Football in the Digital Age: How Online Platforms Are Changing Fan Culture
items.description: Football has always held a special place in Côte d’Ivoire. From crowded stadiums in Abidjan to small community pitches, the sport connects people across generations. Fans follow local clubs, support the national team, and celebrate major victories together. Today, digital technology is changing this experience. Smartphones, social media, live score applications, and online sports platforms give supporters new ways to follow matches and engage with their favourite teams. These changes are especially visible among younger fans, who increasingly combine traditional matchday activities with digital entertainment. Football’s Cultural Importance in Côte d’Ivoire Football remains one of the country’s strongest sources of national pride. The Ivorian national team, widely known as the Elephants, has enjoyed success in African competitions and produced internationally recognised players. One of the most memorable moments came on 11 February 2024, when Côte d’Ivoire won the Africa Cup of Nations on home soil. According to the Confederation of African Football (CAF) , the Elephants came from behind to beat Nigeria 2–1 at a packed Alassane Ouattara Stadium in Abidjan: Franck Kessié equalised after the break and Sébastien Haller scored the winner in the 81st minute, securing a third continental title eight years after the last one. Club football carries the same weight at local level. ASEC Mimosas and Africa Sports have shaped Abidjan’s football culture for decades, and their meetings still divide neighbourhoods, workplaces and families. The Ligue 1 ivoirienne may not attract the television money of European competitions, but it remains the football most supporters can watch in person. Such events show why football continues to play an important role in Ivorian society. However, the way people experience these moments is evolving. How Smartphones Are Transforming Football Fandom In the past, football supporters depended heavily on television, radio, and newspapers for match information. Today, mobile technology provides several additional options: fans can check live scores, receive notifications, watch highlights, and study player statistics without waiting for traditional sports broadcasts. This accessibility is particularly useful for people who cannot watch every match live. Digital services also make it easier to follow international competitions, including the English Premier League, French Ligue 1, UEFA Champions League, and Africa Cup of Nations. Different platforms serve different needs within the modern football experience. Digital platform Main purpose Benefits for football fans Live score apps Match results and statistics Real-time updates and team information Social media News and fan discussions Direct interaction with football communities Video platforms Highlights and interviews Access to football content on demand Sports news websites Reports and analysis Background information and expert commentary Betting comparison websites Comparing sports betting services Information about markets, payments, and platform features Together, these services make following football more flexible and interactive. Social Media Connects Supporters Across Borders Social media has become an important meeting place for football fans. Platforms such as Facebook, WhatsApp, TikTok, and YouTube allow people to discuss matches, share highlights, and exchange opinions about players and coaches. An important goal or controversial referee decision can generate discussions that continue long after the final whistle. These conversations are no longer limited by geography. Ivorian supporters living in Europe or other African countries can participate in the same online communities as fans in Abidjan, Bouaké, or Yamoussoukro. Football clubs also benefit from direct communication with their audiences. Social media helps teams share announcements, promote matches, and maintain relationships with supporters. For smaller clubs, these channels can provide visibility without spending heavily on traditional advertising. What Modern Football Fans Expect From Digital Services As digital platforms become more common, supporters are paying greater attention to convenience, accessibility, and the quality of information. Several features can make online football services more useful: Mobile-friendly design: Websites and applications that work smoothly on smartphones. Real-time information: Quick access to scores, team news, and match statistics. Language accessibility: Content available in French, the main language of communication for many Ivorian supporters. Secure digital services: Clear privacy policies and reliable account protection. Relevant football coverage: Information about African competitions, local clubs, and major European leagues. These expectations influence how fans choose digital platforms, whether they want to read football news, watch highlights, or explore other sports-related services. Sports Betting and the Expansion of Digital Entertainment Online sports betting has also become part of the wider digital football environment. Some adult football supporters use betting services while following domestic and international competitions, and online platforms may provide match statistics, different betting markets, and mobile account management. The practical differences between platforms are local ones. Deposits and withdrawals run mainly through mobile money — Orange Money, MTN MoMo, Moov Money and Wave — rather than bank cards, and transaction fees come straight out of a player’s balance. Competition coverage varies just as much: one operator may concentrate on European football, while another carries more of the Ligue 1 ivoirienne and African tournaments. Supported currencies and account verification procedures also differ. Those are the criteria on which comparisons of the best Ivorian betting sites are useful, rather than the size of a welcome bonus. Users should check whether an operator is authorised to provide services in Côte d’Ivoire rather than assuming that an accessible website is locally licensed. Sports betting also involves financial risks. It should remain an optional activity for adults who meet the legal age requirements, with spending kept within affordable limits. Challenges Facing the Digital Football Experience Although technology offers many benefits, several challenges remain. Internet connectivity and mobile data costs can affect access to streaming services, particularly outside major cities, and not all supporters have smartphones capable of running demanding applications. [INSERT: one verified figure on internet penetration or mobile data cost in Côte d’Ivoire, with a link to the source — see note below.] Another concern is the reliability of online information. False transfer stories, misleading statistics, and unverified rumours can spread quickly through social media, so fans should compare information from different sources before accepting it as accurate. Online security matters just as much. Users need to protect their accounts, avoid suspicious links, and understand how digital platforms handle personal information. Improving digital literacy can help football supporters enjoy new services while reducing unnecessary risks. The Future of Football Fandom in Côte d’Ivoire The relationship between football and technology will likely continue to develop. Improved internet infrastructure could make match broadcasts and live coverage more accessible, and football clubs may invest further in digital ticketing, online merchandise, and direct communication with their audiences. For supporters, these developments could create a more connected and personalised experience. Yet technology is unlikely to replace the excitement of watching football together. Instead, digital platforms are adding new dimensions to an already passionate sporting culture. Whether fans celebrate a goal inside a stadium, follow live updates on a smartphone, or discuss results with friends online, football remains a shared experience. In Côte d’Ivoire, the digital era is simply creating more ways for supporters to stay connected to the sport they love.
