items.title: Tournée diplomatique : le Président Bassirou Diomaye Faye multiplie les initiatives et les partenariats
items.description: De Paris à Phnom Penh, du 9 au 16 novembre 2026, le président de la République a conduit une séquence diplomatique marquée par des échanges avec plusieurs dirigeants et responsables économiques. Au cœur de cette tournée : la consolidation des relations bilatérales, la promotion des intérêts du Sénégal et la recherche d'un consensus autour de la direction de l'Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF). Le président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye, a achevé, le 16 novembre, une tournée diplomatique qui l'a successivement conduit à Paris, en France, puis à Phnom Penh, au Cambodge. Entre rencontres de haut niveau, échanges économiques et participation au 20e Sommet de la Francophonie, ce déplacement a été l'occasion pour le Sénégal de réaffirmer son positionnement sur plusieurs dossiers internationaux et de renforcer ses relations avec ses partenaires. La première étape, du 9 au 12 novembre à Paris, a été marquée par un entretien avec le président français Emmanuel Macron, le 9 novembre, au Palais de l'Élysée. Les deux chefs d'État ont notamment passé en revue les dossiers bilatéraux, avec un accent particulier sur la préparation du Séminaire intergouvernemental et le développement des échanges économiques et commerciaux, dans le cadre du partenariat rénové entre Dakar et Paris. Les discussions ont également porté sur les grandes questions internationales d'intérêt commun. À cette occasion, Bassirou Diomaye Faye a remercié la France pour son appui à l'organisation des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026. Le lendemain, le chef de l'État a pris part, au Palais de Chaillot, à la séquence de haut niveau du Forum de Paris sur la Paix consacrée à la protection de l'enfance. Dans son intervention, il a plaidé pour une protection des enfants sans distinction ni traitement sélectif, notamment dans les contextes de conflit. Il a également mis en avant les engagements du Sénégal en matière de santé, de nutrition et d'éducation, ainsi que sa stratégie nationale de protection de l'enfant et le rôle des familles. La dimension économique a constitué un autre volet important de cette étape parisienne. Le 11 novembre, le président de la République a reçu des dirigeants de groupes industriels et d'institutions financières, notamment Rothschild & Co et Vinci. Les échanges ont porté sur des projets dans les secteurs de l'énergie, de la santé et des infrastructures aéroportuaires, ainsi que sur leurs mécanismes de financement. Le chef de l'État a présenté les priorités du Sénégal et les réformes engagées pour améliorer l'attractivité du pays et renforcer la sécurité des investissements. La seconde étape de cette tournée a conduit le président sénégalais à Phnom Penh, les 15 et 16 novembre, pour le 20e Sommet de la Francophonie, organisé autour du thème « Réinvestir dans la paix pour une prospérité partagée et une stabilité durable ». Cette rencontre a surtout été marquée par les discussions autour de la désignation du prochain secrétaire général de l'OIF. Face aux divergences entre les États membres et à la multiplication des candidatures, le Sénégal a joué un rôle de facilitation pour éviter un scrutin susceptible de fragiliser davantage l'organisation. En amont des décisions, Bassirou Diomaye Faye a réuni les chefs d'État et de gouvernement africains. Cette concertation a permis de rapprocher les positions et d'examiner les conséquences d'un éventuel vote. Le lendemain, devant l'ensemble de ses pairs, le président sénégalais a réaffirmé la neutralité de Dakar dans la compétition entre les candidats, tout en plaidant pour une issue consensuelle. La démarche a débouché sur un compromis : la Secrétaire générale sortante, Louise Mushikiwabo, restera en fonction pendant une année supplémentaire, au terme de laquelle elle ne sollicitera pas un nouveau mandat. Son pays ne présentera pas non plus de candidat. Une nouvelle élection, ouverte aux candidatures, sera organisée à l'issue de cette période. Au-delà de cet épisode institutionnel, le Sénégal a défendu une Francophonie davantage tournée vers la coopération régionale, le dialogue avec les États du Sahel, l'investissement économique et la régulation d'une intelligence artificielle éthique et responsable. Cette orientation s'inscrit notamment dans le contexte de la présidence sénégalaise en exercice de la Communauté économique des États de l'Afrique de l'Ouest (Cedeao). Les travaux du Sommet ont également abouti à l'adoption de la Déclaration de Phnom Penh, qui fixe les orientations de l'organisation pour les prochaines années, d'une résolution sur les situations de crise et la consolidation de la paix dans l'espace francophone, ainsi que de l'Appel de Phnom Penh consacré à la protection du patrimoine et à la diversité culturels. La Déclaration a notamment salué l'organisation, à Dakar, des premiers Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse sur le continent africain. Le Canada accueillera le prochain Sommet en 2028. En marge des travaux, le président de la République a multiplié les rencontres bilatérales. Avec son homologue vietnamien, Tô Lâm, il a évoqué le renforcement de la coopération dans l'agriculture, notamment la riziculture, les télécommunications, la construction, l'industrie automobile, la culture et le sport. Les deux dirigeants ont également relevé les convergences entre la Vision Sénégal 2050 et la stratégie Vietnam 2045. Les échanges avec le Premier ministre du Québec, Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, ont porté sur le renforcement de la coopération bilatérale et l'accroissement des échanges économiques. Le responsable québécois a notamment souligné la stabilité du Sénégal, la qualité de ses institutions et de sa main-d'œuvre, ainsi que sa position géographique, qu'il considère comme des atouts pour en faire une porte d'entrée vers le marché africain. Avec le vice-président de la Confédération suisse, Ignazio Cassis, les discussions ont concerné la formation technique et professionnelle, la coopération scientifique et médicale, les investissements privés, la gestion de l'eau ainsi que les questions de paix et de sécurité. Enfin, l'entretien avec le Premier ministre canadien, Mark Carney, a permis d'aborder les perspectives de coopération dans les domaines de l'économie, de l'agriculture et des investissements, en plus des orientations futures de la Francophonie. À travers cette tournée, le Sénégal a ainsi investi plusieurs espaces de dialogue politique, économique et multilatéral. De Paris à Phnom Penh, le déplacement du chef de l'État a combiné la défense de positions diplomatiques, la recherche de nouveaux partenariats et la promotion des priorités nationales, avec en toile de fond la volonté de consolider la place du Sénégal dans les instances internationales. items.title: Four fake illegal mining taskforce members arrested in Nweneso, 4 others on the run
items.description: National Security operatives have arrested four members of an eight-man criminal syndicate accused of impersonating security personnel to extort large sums of money from small-scale miners at Nweneso Number 2 in the Ashanti Region. The syndicate reportedly operated using two pickup trucks and wore uniforms bearing National Security insignia. They allegedly targeted remote mining communities with limited mobile network coverage, where they posed as security operatives and forced miners to pay large sums of money under the guise of law enforcement. Ashanti Regional Security Liaison Officer, Captain (rtd) Kwame Jabari, identified the four arrested suspects as David Ablor, 51; Samuel Nyarko; Prince Mangomia; and Agyemang Stephen, 34. He said the group had been operating in mining communities for nearly three months, disguising themselves as personnel of National Security, the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) and other security agencies. Speaking to journalists, Captain (rtd) Jabari said the suspects had allegedly extorted substantial amounts of money from unsuspecting miners who believed they were dealing with legitimate security personnel. “Today, we can witness a syndicate who have organized themselves to go round mining areas extorting monies from miners, perpetuating that they are either National Security or other security agencies. And that is what we are facing within the region. In fact, the syndicate that we have arrested has been in the system for almost three months and they have been operating within those mining areas under that disguise. And unfortunately, those innocent miners think they are legitimate security agencies and they have been extorting huge sums of money from them. So, we wanted to let the public know that. Those stories they are saying, this is the actual picture of it. “These boys are an example of it. They are a group of eight people; they have two pickups. Early in the morning or late in the night, they move into a mining area where there is no network or where there is no police access. They go portraying that they are National Security personnel, their National Security personnel, collecting huge sums from miners. By the time they leave the place, they come and tell you it’s National Security who have been there. We have no idea about it. They’ll tell its National Security which have been there. We have no idea about it. But unfortunately for them, the good god that we serve yesterday was their last day,” he said. Captain (rtd) Jabari said his outfit had been monitoring the activities of the group for more than three months following reports of their operations in parts of the Ashanti Region. He told journalists that his outfit received information about the syndicate’s activities in the Atwima Kwanwoma District on Monday, November 16, 2026, through the District Chief Executive. He said a team was immediately dispatched to the area, leading to the arrest of four members of the group. “Yesterday in the evening, I was there and my deputy called me. I also had a call from a National Security personnel within the area that there were some National Security personnel within their area late in the night, around 8 o’clock. So I was a little bit surprised. So I spoke to the district executive, they said we have not sent anybody. I have spoken to the National Commander, he has not sent anybody to that area. So quickly, we dispatched a team to the place, and these are the armed group that we have been chasing for the past three months, we were able to pick them up from the place over there. Unfortunately, we had, they were a group of eight with two pickups, we had one group, we had a pickup; the other group passed a different area. But we have identified one suspect which among them that we know, and we are going to look for them and pick them up.” Meanwhile, the leadership of the Small-Scale Miners Association has urged its members to remain vigilant and report anyone suspected of impersonating security personnel. The association’s spokesperson, Solomon Jabari, advised miners to document the activities of suspicious individuals and promptly alert their leadership. “What we want to entreat all the miners is, they should take pictures or videos of people who visit the sites. However, we know that they have some of our small-scale miners, the leadership, they have their numbers. They should quickly inform them if they see some of these people who come around peddling themselves as National Security from Accra and from various regions, here doing operation. So, I think this is a complete unacceptable. Small-scale miners, let’s all put ourselves together and be able to crack down all these people who are going round impersonating themselves as being National Security or being soldiers or being police people who come to various sites extorting money and huge sums of money from miners.” National Security has since launched a manhunt for the remaining four members of the syndicate who are on the run.

items.title: Tinubu campaigns in Kebbi and pleads with voters to support second-term bid
items.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi President Bola Ahmed Tinubu on Tuesday in Kebbi State appealed to Kebbi voters who gathered at Haliru Abdu Stadium to witness his campaign to obtain permanent voters’ cards to enable them to vote for him in the 2027 general elections. Tinubu, alongside the presidential campaign council, told Kebbi voters to support the candidature of Tinubu and his vice president, Kashi Shettima, to enable them to continue enjoying massive infrastructure already being executed in Kebbi state, which he said is evidence of federal presence. “I thank you from the bottom of my heart, the people of Kebbi State, for enduring the blazing sun to welcome me in Kebbi State. I urge you all to get your PVCs to vote for me, the governor, and other APC candidates in Kebbi State.” The president added that he was in Kebbi during the last elections; he is here again to thank Kebbi voters for their massive support in the last polls and appealed to them to do so in 2027. He pledged to continue his job in education security, healthcare and agriculture, describing it as a catalyst for food security in the country. Earlier, the presidential campaign director general of the ruling All Progressives Congress, Senator Abdul Aziz Yarima, challenged the opposition candidate to tell the people of the north what he did to them when he was at helm of affairs. Yari pointed out that Tinubu is the real lover of the north because of the massive infrastructure presence in the region. He urged the opposition in the country to reconsider their claims that Tinubu has no support in the north, saying no president in Nigeria has developed the north like president Tinubu. Yari appealed to Northwest voters not to be carried away by the lies of the opposition, who think the APC doesn’t have support in the north. In his welcome address, the governor of Kebbi state, Dr Nasir Idris, thanked the president for the presidential campaign rally in Kebbi state. He assured the president that Kebbi is for Tinubu and APC, for him as governor and all the candidates of the ruling party. “Mr President, what you are witnessing now tells you that Kebbi is for you, for APC, for me and all our candidates.” Idris pledged to deliver APC for Tinubu in the one hundred percent of the 2027 elections, saying the people of Kebbi state are eager to repay the good works of the president for the state. While commending his efforts in agriculture, security, education and healthcare, he appealed to him to grant full operation of Tsamiya inland dry port to boost economic activities in the state; the request was granted by the mister president. Kebbi rally was attended by three former Kebbi governors, serving budget minister Atiku Bagudu, APC National Chairman Netenwe, Senator Adams Oshimole, Senate President Godwill Apkabio, Speaker of the National Assembly, Abass Tajjudeen, former APC National Chairman, Vice President Kashi Shettima, Senator Remi Tinubu and top APC brass. The post Tinubu campaigns in Kebbi and pleads with voters to support second-term bid appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 8 Pakistan Bar Council members call on judiciary to take note of Imran's plea for medical treatment
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Eight members of the Pakistan Bar Council (PBC) on Tuesday called upon the judiciary to ensure implementation of the Supreme Court’s (SC) order directing incarcerated ex-premier Imran Khan’s transfer to Shifa International Hospital for medical treatment. On Aug 18 , a three-member SC bench had directed the government to shift Imran to SIH within the next two days as it heard several petitions concerning his health. However, the government took the PTI founder to the government-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences for a check-up and then transported him back to prison. On Monday, in an open letter to the chief justices of the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC), the SC and the Islamabad High Court (IHC), Imran appealed for medical treatment for himself and Bushra Bibi. He also said that he would only be able to prove his innocence in the various cases against him “if I stay alive”. In a statement issued on Tuesday, eight members of the PBC said: “We call upon the judiciary to take up the former prime minister’s plea immediately and to save his and his wife’s lives by ensuring that court orders are implemented, that proper medical treatment is provided and that due process and a fair trial are guaranteed as mandated by the Constitution.” The statement was signed by Abid Shahid Zuberi, Muhammad Maqsood Buttar, Shafqat Mehmood Chauhan, Abdul Sattar Khan, Munir Ahmed Kakar, Salman Akram Raja, Salahuddin Ahmed and Qazi Muhammad Arshad. The PBC members urged the government and its agencies to implement court orders and ensure that both Imran and his wife received proper medical treatment in accordance with the law and the Constitution. The statement warned that the government and its agencies would be solely responsible for “imperilling” the lives and liberty of the couple. “We the undersigned reserve our right to initiate legal proceedings to protect the life, liberty, and constitutional and legal rights of Imran and Bushra Bibi,” the statement said. The statement also condemned “in the strongest terms” the alleged unlawful and unconstitutional treatment meted out to Imran and his wife, adding that the situation was endangering their lives, liberty and dignity. “[Imran’s] letter reveals that the former prime minister and his wife have been denied their constitutional and human rights through trumped-up and false cases and that they are incarcerated in violation of the law, the jail manual and the prison rules,” the statement asserted. The statement further added that Imran and Bushra Bibi were convicted in false cases and their appeals against these convictions had not been heard. “Even their bail applications have not been fixed for hearing,” it said. The statement further highlighted that Imran had been kept in solitary confinement and denied due medical treatment and access to his legal team and family members, jeopardising his and his wife’s health. The statement also alleged that his sisters had been detained arbitrarily and unlawfully, while the SC’s Aug 18 order had been openly flouted by the government and its agencies in violation of the law and the Constitution. “Every person in Pakistan is guaranteed the right to life and liberty under Article 9, and the right to due process and a fair trial under Article 10-A of the Constitution,” the statement said. “These rights have been denied to Imran, his wife, his family and his party members,” it said. “As patriotic Pakistanis who believe in the rule of law, we are ashamed to read Imran’s plea for implementation of the SC’s orders and for the proper medical treatment that has been denied to him and his wife,” the statement said. Moreover, the Democratic Alliance, a confederation of lawyers led by former PBC vice chairman Abid Saqi, expressed grave alarm over what it described as the deteriorating health and unlawful detention conditions of Imran and his family members. In a statement, the alliance asked the judiciary to take immediate notice of the matter and enforce its orders concerning medical treatment and access to family members. It also called on the government to end Imran’s solitary confinement, provide him with comprehensive medical treatment and release family members held without cause. The alliance’s statement further urged the international community and human rights organisations to take urgent cognisance of the “grave” situation. “The life of a former prime minister and his family hang in the balance. Justice delayed is justice denied. The Democratic Alliance demands that the rule of law and human dignity prevail before it is too late,” the statement said. Separately, the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan also expressed “deep concern” at what it called the state’s treatment of political prisoners, urging authorities to uphold their fundamental rights, irrespective of political affiliation. Referring to the allegations Imran made in his letter, the HRCP said they required urgent and independent examination. “HRCP stresses that violations of political prisoners’ fundamental freedoms are not a matter of personalities or political affiliations; they constitute an assault on the rule of law,” the commission said. “Every prisoner is entitled to humane treatment, adequate healthcare, access to family and lawyers, and a fair trial. All relevant court orders must be implemented and allegations of mistreatment independently investigated,” it added.

items.title: 'Under the bus': Feuds grip Trump's White House after midterms
items.description: From feuding officials stuck together on Air Force One to uncomfortable press conferences, rifts in President Donald Trump’s White House have spilt into the open after the US midterm elections . Disagreements over China, AI and Iran have flared up, while personal rivalries in the West Wing that were bottled up for the first half of Trump’s second term have started to boil over. Most public of all is the feud between Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, over the scandal involving an alleged Chinese spy that forced Nvidia’s Jensen Huang to resign . Bessent delivered an astonishing slap-down in an interview on CNBC on Friday when he openly rebuked Lutnick’s department for failing to blacklist Megaspeed, a company formerly linked to Huang’s lover that was accused of shifting vital Nvidia chips to China. “Bessent just threw Lutnick under the bus, ran over him, backed up, and ran over him again,” Washington Post analyst Josh Rogin wrote on X. The squabbling pair were then forced to spend nearly 20 awkward hours together in the presidential jet as Trump travelled to Asia. On the ground in Manila on Tuesday, Lutnick and Bessent studiously ignored each other despite being seated side by side while Trump signed a trade deal with Thailand. ‘Two different views’ Trump played down the row and denied that he planned to fire Lutnick. Yet at the same time he admitted a rift at the heart of his administration’s China policy just days before a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen. “They’re fine. They have two different views,” Trump told an AFP reporter as he left the White House on Monday when asked about Bessent and Lutnick’s relationship. “One wants to be friendly with China, and one wants to have a blow-up with China.” The White House denied any disunity. “President Trump has assembled the most talented and impressive cabinet in history and they are doing an excellent job carrying out the President’s agenda. Efforts by the legacy media to sow internal division is a distraction that will not work,” White House spokesman Davis Ingle said in a statement to AFP . “All agencies across this administration have and will continue to be in lockstep with President Trump’s mission to deliver results for the American people.” The midterms have already claimed their first scalp in the West Wing, after Trump named immigration hardliner Stephen Miller to replace so-called “ice maiden” Susie Wiles as his chief of staff. And there has been jockeying for position as speculation swirls about who could be next. ‘Besties’ An example came on Friday as Trump’s administration struggled to get to grips with a mass air travel shutdown. The White House put Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Homeland Security chief Markwayne Mullin at the podium in front of reporters — but their double act did not entirely go to plan. Duffy appeared to shake his head and gently nudge his colleague’s elbow when Mullin said that new “patches” were overwhelming old equipment — contradicting the transport chief’s assertion that it was only the ageing gear that was to blame. The Iran war has also been a source of tension. Vice President JD Vance said the day after the midterms that “ the reason we lost is the war ,” apparently seeking to distance himself from the conflict ahead of a possible presidential run in 2028. Trump denied Vance’s comments had affected their relationship. Yet he told reporters on Nov 8 that “a lot of people didn’t like his comments” — before adding: “But not me.” Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth, who has fought off an impeachment bid for now over the Iran war, also subtly sought to distance himself from Vance’s comments. “I respect the vice president greatly, and I’m certainly not going to engage in any finger-pointing,” Hegseth said last week, before adding that the Iran war was “not necessarily popular, but it may have been necessary.” Still, it’s not all knives out at the White House. Miller, the new chief of staff, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio have struck up an “unlikely alliance” after being foes during Trump’s first term, the Wall Street Journal reported. Miller’s wife, Katie, told the paper that the two men were now “besties”.

items.title: 2027 Budget good but fiscal target difficult to attain – Cynergy Global
items.description: Cynergy Global Holding, an investment bank, has described the 2027 Budget as a good one, but the fiscal target is difficult to attain, saying revenue must double twice as fast as the economy In its review of the 2027 Budget, it said Ghana missed its tax-to-Gross Domestic Product target in every year from 2018 to 2023. Again, in the first nine months of 2025, oil receipts were 52.2% below target and non-oil tax revenue was 4.1% below target. However, in 2026, total revenue is 3.5% above target after ten months. This, it said, supports the government’s claim that compliance and technology reforms work. “At the July to October average of GH¢23.6 billion per month, 2026 revenue is about GH¢266 billion (our calculation). The 2026 Budget target is GH¢268.1 billion. The Budget phasing for January to October suggests a higher target for the last two months. November and December receipts will determine the full-year result”, it said. It stated that the 2027 target is steep, highlighting that implied nominal GDP grows by about 13% in 2027 in its calculation from the 17.9% ratio. Therefore, revenue must grow by about 21% against the 2026 estimate. This means revenue must grow about 1.7 times as fast as nominal GDP. According to Cynergy Global, the measures declared in the budget are small compared with the gap. “Approved reforms and compliance give 0.5% of GDP. The target increase from the 2026 Budget is 1.1 percentage points. Government must also rely on growth, oil prices and gold”. It added that the 2027 Budget gives no cost for the solar panel and battery exemptions or for the other incentives. Each one reduces the base that the government must collect from. Transfers to statutory and earmarked funds are estimated at GH¢76.5 billion in 2027. They were, however, GH¢53.7 billion from January to October 2026. It said uncapping the Communications Service Tax and Ghana EXIM Bank levies adds to this, adding, less revenue stays free for other priorities. Expenditure Management The government expenditure on a commitment basis amounted to GHS239.0 billion in the first ten months of 2026, representing 15.0% of GDP and 7.6% below target. Cynergy Global acknowledged that all expenditure categories stayed within programmed limits. Spending was concentrated in compensation, grants and interest payments, together about 68% of total expenditure. Compensation remained the largest item, which limits resources available for discretionary spending and development priorities. Interest payments stood at GHS38.8 billion, 16% of total expenditure, against a target of GHS51.5 billion. Interest as a share of domestic revenue declined from 25.6% to 17.8% by October 2026, reflecting reduced coupon payments on restructured domestic debt and easing borrowing costs. Sustaining the savings will be important to preserve fiscal space. Capital expenditure is GHS41.4 billion, 17% of total expenditure, against a programmed GHS45.3 billion, pointing to a fast pace of public investment execution. The World Bank estimates indicate about US$37.2 billion in annual investment is required to close Ghana’s infrastructure gap. Cynergy Global said the planned increase in capital expenditure is an opportunity to accelerate progress in closing Ghana’s infrastructure gap, particularly in energy and transport. The 2027 Budget allocates GHS100.4 billion to capital expenditure, 5.6% of GDP and about 25.8% of total planned expenditure. It argued that the impact will depend on project selection, implementation readiness and value for money.

items.title: GCB Bank records GH¢2.87bn profit before tax in nine months to September
items.description: Loans grow 47.7%, non-performing loans ratio falls to 4.8%, while earnings per share rise 43.3%. Bank targets at least GH¢3.7bn profit before tax for 2026. GCB Bank PLC recorded a profit before tax of GH¢2.87 billion for the nine months to September 2026, representing a 42.6 per cent increase over the same period last year. The figure is equivalent to 91 per cent of the Bank’s full-year profit before tax for 2025. Presenting its Facts Behind the Figures to investors and analysts, the bank attributed its performance to increased lending, growth in non-funded income and improved operational efficiency, against a backdrop of declining interest rates and pressure on lending margins. The results come as GCB implements its 2025–2028 strategy, which seeks to expand its lending activities, diversify income sources and improve operational performance. Deposits support business growth Customer deposits increased by 22.9 per cent to GH¢50.78 billion, with Current and Savings Accounts (CASA) accounting for 93.2 per cent of the bank’s total funding mix during the period. The Retail, Wholesale and Investment Banking (WIB), and Commercial and Business Banking (CBB) divisions all contributed to deposit growth. Lending expands The growth in deposits supported an expansion in the bank’s lending activities and total assets. Total assets increased by 29 per cent year-to-date to GH¢67.62 billion, while gross loans rose by 47.7 per cent to GH¢26.33 billion. This represents a 120.6 per cent increase in gross loans since December 2024. Loans now account for 47.4 per cent of the bank’s earning assets, compared with 40.6 per cent at the end of 2024. The bank also reported an improvement in its Non-Performing Loans (NPLs) ratio, which declined to 4.8 per cent from 10.8 per cent a year earlier and 15.06 per cent at the end of 2024. The NPL ratio improved across all three business divisions, according to the bank. Non-funded income drives earnings Non-funded income, comprising fees, trading and foreign exchange earnings, increased by 81.7 per cent to GH¢2.13 billion. It accounted for 37.4 per cent of operating income, an increase of 10.1 percentage points over the previous year. Total operating income rose by 32.4 per cent to GH¢5.70 billion, despite pressure on margins from declining interest rates. Operating costs increased by 21.3 per cent, resulting in a positive operating jaws of 11.1 percentage points, as income growth outpaced cost growth. The cost-to-income ratio improved to 45.1 per cent from 47.9 per cent at the end of 2024. The bank’s annualised return on equity stood at 36.3 per cent, while return on assets was 4.1 per cent. Earnings per share increased by 43.3 per cent to GH¢9.38. GCB’s shares also recorded gains on the stock market, nearly doubling in value year-to-date, according to the bank. Management comments Managing Director of GCB Bank PLC, Mr Farihan Alhassan, said the results reflected the bank’s decision to expand lending to businesses and households while diversifying its income sources and controlling costs. “These results show what disciplined execution can do,” he said. “The easy Treasury era is over, and we saw it coming. We chose to lend more to Ghanaian businesses, to earn more from serving customers well, and to spend every cedi with care. The outcome is a bank that is larger, more productive, more diversified, and cleaner. Our customers trust us with their deposits, and we are putting that trust to work for Ghana’s growth.” 2026 outlook Based on its performance to September 2026 and prevailing operating assumptions, management is targeting a minimum profit before tax of GH¢3.7 billion for the 2026 financial year. The bank noted that the outlook remains subject to changes in interest rates, credit conditions, market activity and other factors affecting its operating environment.

items.title: Wawa : La radio rurale « Ibanu » officiellement lancée
items.description: Badou, 17 nov. (ATOP) – La radio rurale « Ibanu » installée dans la commune Wawa 1 a été inauguré, le lundi 16 novembre à Badou. La cérémonie de lancement des émissions de cette radio rurale « Ibanu, la voix de Wawa » émettant sur la fréquence 87.9 FM, a été présidée par le directeur national des radios rurales, Wiyao Amayi, représentant du ministre de la Communication. Elle a été marquée par la présentation du bureau du comité local de gestion de la station, placé sous la présidence de Boni Sabi, la coupure du ruban, la visite guidée des installations techniques, comprenant le studio d’animation, la salle technique et l’émetteur. L’historique du jumelage entre la commune Wawa 1 et le département de la Vienne, ayant conduit à la concrétisation de ce projet d’installation de cette radio communautaire a été retracée. Le directeur national des radios rurales, a lancé un appel à l’ensemble des forces vives et des acteurs du développement local afin qu’ils soutiennent le personnel dans l’accomplissement de sa noble mission. M. Amayi a rappelé que cet outil de communication a pour vocation essentielle d’informer, d’éduquer et de mobiliser les communautés dans leurs langues locales, favorisant ainsi l’essor socio-économique, la cohésion sociale et la valorisation du patrimoine culturel. Le préfet de Wawa, Djimbondjo Bintiene Laré, le maire de Wawa 1, Tchamdja Bawubadi Malaki, et le président des chefs traditionnels de Wawa, Folly IV, ont testé les nouveaux équipements en s’adressant directement à leurs administrés à travers les ondes de la nouvelle station. Coupure du ruban symbolique Le préfet Djimbondjo a émis le vœu de voir la radio s’acquitter pleinement de sa mission républicaine en consolidant la paix, l’harmonie sociale et le développement durable de la commune, voire de la préfecture. Il a exhorté l’équipe dirigeante et technique à la rigueur professionnelle et au strict respect des règles éthiques et déontologiques inhérentes au métier d’informateur. Cet événement s’est déroulé en présence des personnalités administratives, politiques et coutumières, d’une délégation française du département de la Vienne, partenaire technique et financier conduite par M. Bruno Grignard, aux côtés de Firmin Ossobè, président de l’association CASO Togo, dont l’entremise a été déterminante dans la concrétisation de ce partenariat fructueux entre la commune Wawa 1 et la collectivité territoriale française. ATOP/PM/KKT/BA

items.title: 80-year-old woman rescued after alleged ritual attempt to behead her in Ashanti Region
items.description: An 80-year-old woman has been rescued by residents after unknown assailants attacked her at Nyankyerenease in the Kwadaso Municipality of the Ashanti Region. Residents alleged that the assailants attempted to behead the aged woman for ritual purposes. The victim, who is yet to be identified, was reportedly attacked in her room on Monday, November 16, 2026. A resident, who spoke to Adom News, said the woman was found seriously injured with her neck slit open and lying in her room on the day of the incident. “We woke up in the morning only to see the woman seriously injured in her room,” the resident said. According to residents, the suspects fled after the attack, leaving the woman in a critical condition. Neighbours quickly intervened and rushed to her aid. The aged woman has since been rushed to the Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital for surgery and other critical medical care. Police in the area have also been notified to investigate the matter, as residents appeal to the security agency to intensify patrols in the area to protect lives, especially the elderly.

items.title: Mahama to unveil new DNA, vaccine research laboratories at Noguchi
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama is expected to commission new human DNA testing laboratories and a dedicated vaccine development facility at the Noguchi Memorial Institute for Medical Research (NMIMR) on Wednesday, November 18. The facilities are aimed at strengthening Ghana’s capacity to conduct essential medical and scientific investigations locally and reduce dependence on foreign laboratories for the analysis of critical samples. The Ministry of Health announced the planned commissioning in a Facebook post on Tuesday, November 17, describing the investment as an important step towards building the country’s domestic scientific and research capabilities. According to the Ministry, recent experiences have highlighted the need for Ghana to develop the capacity to undertake critical laboratory tests within the country rather than rely on sending samples abroad for analysis. The new laboratories are expected to improve the country’s capabilities in human DNA testing and vaccine research, while enhancing preparedness for public health emergencies. “Tomorrow, President John Dramani Mahama will commission new DNA Laboratories for human testing, alongside a dedicated laboratory for vaccine development at the Noguchi Memorial Institute for Medical Research (NMIMR),” the Ministry stated. The commissioning ceremony is scheduled for 2:00 p.m. on Wednesday at the institute in Accra.

items.title: Bola Ray featured in GQ Poland, says Africa is not the next big thing, Africa is now
items.description: Renowned media mogul and CEO of EIB Network, Nathan Kwabena Anokye Adisi, popularly known as Bola Ray, has been featured in the 2026 edition of GQ Poland’s GQ Business magazine in a wide-ranging interview titled “Własnym głosem” (“In His Own Voice”). The multi-page feature, published in the magazine’s Business World section, was conducted by Omenaa Mensah, founder of the Omenaa Art Foundation, Omenaa Foundation and TOP CHARITY, with photography by Jacek Poremba. It traces Bola Ray’s journey from student radio DJ to head of one of Ghana’s leading media groups. He told the magazine that he began his career in the late 1990s as a volunteer at Radio Universe at the University of Ghana, where he studied management. He explained that his stage name came about when he entered Accra Academy at age 11. “Bola” stands for “brilliant, outstanding, loving, ambitious,” while “Ray” stands for “religious, ambitious, young.” He said he set out to become the biggest DJ in Ghana and the first with a degree, at a time when many believed the profession was for people without formal education. “I wanted to change that stereotype,” he said. “Africa is now” On the continent’s place in the world, Bola Ray said Africa is largely undiscovered and has many stories to tell, and he urged foreign media to give it far more attention. He said the world hears too often about hunger, war, poverty and disease, when Africa is a jewel of enormous potential. He asked why stories of Afrobeats conquering the world, and of Africa’s music and creative industries, are not told more often. “There are reports saying Africa is ‘the next big thing.’ I disagree. Africa is now,” he said. He pointed to the continent’s natural resources, including lithium, cocoa, gold and diamonds, and called on industrialists and entrepreneurs to build factories in Africa to add value locally. A call for collaboration and positive stories Bola Ray said he would like to see genuine collaboration among African media houses in countries such as Nigeria, Ghana, South Africa and Kenya, working together each week to select the most important African story and share it with their audiences. He noted that the media is no longer limited to traditional companies, as anyone with a phone can tell the story of their community, culture or place. He also stressed the need to showcase success stories from Africa and the diaspora, which inspired him to create the television programme Revealed . “We cannot talk endlessly about politics. We must tell positive stories as well,” he said. He observed that Africans have for years been taught not to talk too much about their achievements for fear of seeming arrogant, and said he wants experienced African entrepreneurs to share their stories with young people. “It is good to appear in Western media, but it is equally important to tell these stories here,” he said. Omenaa Sport & Art Campus Bola Ray also spoke about the Omenaa Sport & Art Campus in Tema, which opened in October, and praised Omenaa Mensah for an initiative that supports young talent in Africa. He said he wants young people to meet artists, entrepreneurs and others who can become role models. “It is not about boasting of success, but about showing them what is possible,” he said. .

items.title: Kozah : Des artisans membres de la CMR KARA en formation sur la technique de soudure MIG MAG
items.description: Kara, 17 nov. (ATOP) – Les artisans soudeurs de la Kozah, membres de la Chambre régionale de métiers de la Kara (CRM-Kara), participent du 16 au 21 novembre à Kara, à un atelier de formation sur la soudure MIG MAG, fortement utilisé aujourd’hui en milieu industriel. La formation est à l’actif de la CRM-Kara avec l’appui technique et financier du Fonds national d’apprentissage, de formation et de perfectionnement professionnels (FNAFPP). Elle intervient dans le cadre d’un projet collectif de perfectionnement des artisanats membres de la chambre régionale de métiers. L’objectif est d’initier les participants sur la modernisation de l’activité de la soudure, notamment l’intégration de la soudure moderne (MAG) à la soudure classique (MIG), pour mieux répondre aux exigences du marché industriel de la soudure, devenu très compétitif. La finalité est de faire d’eux des formateurs de leurs pairs en vue d’être plus autonomes et plus compétitifs au niveau local et régional, voire national. La session de formation est placée sous le thème : « Les chambres de métiers du Togo, précurseurs de la digitalisation ! Soyez dans cette logique et partager cette information autour de vous. Ensemble pour un secteur créateur de richesse ! ». Elle regroupe notamment un échantillon d’artisans soudeurs de la préfecture de la Kozah, exerçant dans la carrosserie. Le chef d’antenne FNAFPP Kara, Lochina Moussa Mahamadou, représentant le président du comité de gestion de l’institution, a souligné que la formation répond à un besoin exprimé par les professionnels de la région. « Le choix de consacrer cette session à la soudure MIG-MAG n’est pas anodin, ses procédés largement utilisés en milieu industriel pour leur efficacité et leur polyvalence, constituent des compétences techniques incontournables dans les métiers de la construction métallique et de la carrosserie », a-t-il expliqué. Le président des formateurs, Letou Kobietema, a rappelé aux bénéficiaires l’importance capitale de la formation, les invitant à être attentifs et participatifs pour une restitution fidèle et facile à leurs camarades qui n’ont pas la chance d’être sélectionnés. Le représentant du maire Kozah 1, M. Aklesso Kpatcha, et le président de la CRM Kara, Able Kpatcha, ont assisté à l’ouverture des travaux. ATOP/LER/TAL/MD

Bas-mono : Un bâtiment scolaire amélioré bientôt à l’EPP Ahonto-Kopé
items.description: Afagnagan, 17 nov. (ATOP) – Les travaux de construction d’un bâtiment scolaire amélioré de trois salles de classe ont été lancés, le lundi 16 novembre, à l’école primaire publique (EPP) Ahonto-Kopé, dans la commune de Bas-Mono 2. Ce projet est une initiative de la mairie de la commune de Bas-Mono 2. Il s’intègre dans la dynamique de sa politique d’amélioration des infrastructures éducatives en vue du renforcement des capacités d’accueil. Le futur bâtiment comprendra trois salles de classe spacieuses et bien aérées, une direction, et sera réalisé selon les normes en vigueur pour offrir aux élèves et aux enseignants un cadre d’apprentissage adéquat. L’objectif est de contribuer à améliorer les conditions d’apprentissage et d’étude des apprenants et le travail des enseignants. Il s’agit d’offrir un cadre plus adapté et confortable aux apprenants. La cérémonie de lancement a été marquée par le premier coup de pelle du sénateur, maire de la commune Bas-Mono 2, Afangbédji Komlanvi Sédoufia. Elle a mobilisé les autorités éducatives, traditionnelles, les parents, les élèves ainsi que les forces vives de la localité. Le sénateur Afangbédji a rappelé la priorité que le conseil municipal de la commune de Bas-Mono 2 accorde à l’éducation, socle de tout développement. Il a insisté sur la qualité des ouvrages et invité l’entreprise à respecter le délai d’exécution des travaux. Le maire a exhorté la communauté à accompagner l’entreprise à travers certains travaux et à suivre de près le chantier. Les autorités éducatives, les enseignants, les parents et les élèves ont pris part cette inauguration. ATOP/DK/MD

items.title: Xi’s Heavy-Handedness May Be Backfiring
items.description: Asian countries hoping to resist China’s ambitions for regional supremacy might look to a recent art festival in South Korea for inspiration. The Gwangju Biennale, founded in 1994 to celebrate Asian culture and South Korea’s democracy, erupted in controversy in September over the organizers’ decision to grant Taiwan its own self-named pavilion—in defiance of Beijing’s purported claims to the island. But despite the Chinese Foreign Ministry’s demands that the South Korean authorities rectify this “ grave violation ,” the Biennale’s organizers refused to budge. China’s unappeased delegation pulled out of the festival in a huff. The incident offered the other attendees a valuable lesson: China needn’t always get its way. China’s neighbors would do well to keep this in mind during this week’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. On its surface, the annual gathering of leaders of countries throughout the Pacific region, including the United States, will be a showcase of China’s growing power. As the summit’s host, Chinese President Xi Jinping has savvily invited his guests to the tech hub Shenzhen, home to leading robotics manufacturers, the telecommunications firm Huawei, top drone makers, and roving robotaxis. Meanwhile, President Trump, Xi’s main counterweight in the region, will arrive tomorrow as a diminished figure—unpopular at home, entangled in a costly and controversial war abroad, and presiding over a party that voters just cast out of Congress. Washington’s traditional allies in the region have already been rattled by Trump’s unexpected turn toward China in his second term. Countries such as Australia are now working to figure out how to protect themselves against China’s encroaching power without the assurance of American support. “If the U.S. isn’t there, we are going to be a little bit more circumspect about how we stand up to China,” Gordon Flake, the chief executive of the Perth USAsia Centre at the University of Western Australia, told me. “But it doesn’t mean we won’t do it.” Unlike European leaders, who are similarly trying to defend their interests against China amid a breakdown in the Atlantic alliance, the countries of Asia lack a unifying body to coordinate policy or assert collective power. The European Union can press Beijing for concessions on trade with Europe’s common market, but the Pacific region’s various governments must negotiate deals on their own. Compared with EU members, these countries are also more politically and economically diverse—some are wealthy and some are poor; some are democracies and some are not. This makes delivering a single unified message more challenging. More than 70 percent of people in Malaysia, Singapore, and Indonesia view China favorably, compared with less than 30 percent in South Korea and India, and 11 percent in Japan, according to survey data from the Pew Research Center. [ Read: China’s intelligence coup in the AI war ] Yet the stakes for countering China’s rise are higher in Asia than anywhere else. China’s economy is far and away the most dominant in the region—more than four times that of Japan, Asia’s second-biggest economy. Xi has worked to project China’s power throughout the world, but he is most interested in ruling over his own neighborhood. As he declared in a pivotal 2014 speech that marked the country’s turn toward a more assertive regional policy, “It is for the people of Asia to run the affairs of Asia, solve the problems of Asia, and uphold the security of Asia,” in clear opposition to foreign interference in the region. “The Chinese people, in their pursuit of the Chinese dream of great national renewal, stand ready to support and help other peoples in Asia to realize their own great dreams.” Most countries in the region would prefer to realize their own dreams without China’s “support.” Despite Trump’s inconsistent approach to maintaining ties with long-standing allies, countries such as Japan, South Korea, and Australia are wary of partnering with Xi’s new imperial order instead. Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, having touted the importance of “a multipolar Asia,” dismissed the Asia-for-Asians idea as unrealistic in 2022: “A narrow Asian chauvinism is actually against the continent’s own interest.” India’s leaders have good reason to resist China’s ambitions, which have involved expanding its economic and military influence into South Asia, testing New Delhi’s resolve along their shared Himalayan border, and supporting Pakistan, India’s bitter rival. Beijing “thinks that India needs to accept subordinate status to China,” Manoj Joshi, a fellow at the Observer Research Foundation in New Delhi, told me. But “India is not willing to accept that in any way it is second to China.” Beijing’s contentious territorial claims have other neighbors on edge as well. Xi’s extensive military drills around Taiwan have raised fears of a devastating regional war. His insistent claim to nearly all of the South China Sea keeps China in almost-constant conflict with the Philippines. In July, the Philippine government accused China’s coast guard of allegedly injuring a Filipino sailor in the South China Sea, lamenting in a statement : “We simply cannot trust this belligerent neighbor.” Last month, the Chinese ambassador in Manila drew sharp criticism for provocatively claiming that China “may easily win” a war against the Philippines—though he denied that he was making a threat. Xi has attempted to soften these political conflicts with promises of economic cooperation, but any hope that China’s rise would lift other countries has faded. The same state-subsidized Chinese exports that have threatened industries in the United States and Europe have undercut various sectors throughout Asia as well. Trade with Southeast Asian countries accounts for nearly a quarter of China’s global trade surplus. Chinese companies are expanding their market share in manufacturing industries that are central to South Korea’s economy, such as shipbuilding, batteries, and petrochemicals. Xi has sought to use China’s growing economic might to coerce neighbors to concede to his political demands. Beijing halted supplies of rare earth elements to Japan in January after Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi warned that a Chinese invasion of Taiwan could trigger a military response. (Despite this pressure, Japan has not withdrawn its comment.) Even as Trump has cozied up to Xi over the past year, his administration has tried to reassure Asian allies of its continued support. The U.S. conducted naval drills with the Philippines and Japan in the South China Sea in July. Just before this year’s APEC summit, Trump met with his fellow leaders from Australia, India, and Japan for talks about enhanced cooperation on AI, critical minerals, and maritime security, with new plans for joint military exercises to counter China’s power. But other moves add to traditional U.S. allies’ unease. Trump has delayed approval of a $14 billion arms sale to Taiwan, presumably to stay on better terms with Xi. Last year Trump flew all the way to South Korea to meet with Xi on the sidelines of the APEC summit, but skipped the summit itself. In the absence of clear signals from Washington, Asian leaders have tightened ties with one another. In 2017, when Trump withdrew from the Trans-Pacific Partnership, a regional trade pact designed to isolate China, the other 11 members moved forward without the United States. Japan has expanded its relationships in the region, in part by offering aid to strengthen the defense capabilities of other Asian countries. Australia and India have deepened their collaboration through expanded intelligence-sharing and joint military exercises. [ Read: The future of AI is not China ] But leaders in the region must tread carefully. They all have close trade links to China and can’t risk alienating their vindictive neighbor. Akio Takahara, an expert on diplomacy at Tokyo Woman’s Christian University, told me that Chinese leaders actively “try to disturb any attempt by other countries to link up.” Ironically, the more powerful China becomes, the more necessary the U.S. is as a counterweight. Flake told me that although there is “acute concern about the reliability of the United States,” policy makers in Australia still view this alliance as crucial to the country’s security—and “there is no clear Plan B.” Instead, they are “striving to get the United States back to where the United States has been.” The fact that the U.S. is still indispensable in Asia indicates the extent of Xi’s failure to dominate the region. Trump’s unpredictable foreign policy has delivered Xi a chance to expand Chinese influence at America’s expense, but the Chinese leader’s heavy-handed pursuit of power has ultimately left the door open for a U.S. revival in his own backyard. Instead of treating his neighbors like imperial subjects, Xi might consider letting Chinese artists participate in the Gwangju Biennale next time and enjoy the party.

items.title: COP31: Advocates urge funders to double clean air money for Africa, Asia and Latin America by COP32
items.description: Clean air advocates at COP31 have urged philanthropic funders to double their annual support for air quality initiatives in Africa, Latin America and parts of Asia, warning that inadequate financing is undermining efforts to tackle pollution in some of the world’s most affected regions. The advocates say the three regions, excluding China and India, currently receive a combined US$8.3 million annually in philanthropic funding for clean air work. They want that amount increased to about US$16 million a year, with more resources directed towards locally led monitoring systems, research and the use of air quality data in policymaking. The call was made during a session on financing clean air in the Global South, co-hosted by Sustenta Honduras and Clean Energy Nepal in Antalya, Türkiye, on November 13. Opening the session, Sustenta Honduras Executive Director Ricardo said the discussion was intended to demonstrate how locally generated air quality data could influence public policy and government spending. “We want to show what implementation looks like when air quality data produced in country reaches the people who set the policies and budget,” he said. Christa Hasenkopf, Director of the Clean Air Program and Founder of the EPIC Air Quality Fund at the University of Chicago’s Energy Policy Institute, said fine particulate matter pollution (PM2.5) contributes to about eight million deaths annually and is the world’s second-leading health risk factor, behind high blood pressure. She cited World Bank estimates that the health damage associated with PM2.5 pollution costs the global economy about US$8.1 trillion. Despite the scale of the problem, Hasenkopf said less than 0.1 per cent of global philanthropic funding goes towards clean air initiatives, citing the Clean Air Fund. “If you look at Africa, it receives less than a million dollars a year on average for clean air work. Yet PM2.5 kills more folks than HIV/AIDS, or malaria,” she said. International development funding is also limited. The Clean Air Fund’s State of Global Air Quality Funding 2026 report found that less than one per cent of international development funding is directed specifically towards outdoor air pollution. The report also found that 89 per cent of air quality funding between 2020 and 2024 was provided as loans. However, a report by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and the Climate and Clean Air Coalition, Hidden Assets , estimates that every US$1 invested in measures addressing air pollution and climate change together generates about US$15 in returns. Hasenkopf challenged funders to help close the financing gap before the next climate summit. “If you look at philanthropic funding for clean air in Asia excluding China and India, Africa and Latin America combined, it’s US$8.3 million a year. We can double that,” she said. She said the immediate target was to raise annual funding for the three regions to about US$16 million, arguing that a small number of major funders could help achieve the increase. “Probably just a couple funders … could double that amount across the world and it’d be incredibly meaningful,” she said, suggesting that grants of between US$50,000 and US$100,000 per project would be a useful starting point. “This is changeable by next COP, I believe,” she added. Hasenkopf also stressed that funding should strengthen air quality monitoring capacity in the countries affected by pollution rather than leave them dependent on external programmes. She cited a US State Department initiative that installed air quality monitors at diplomatic missions in 38 countries and, according to research, contributed to reductions in PM2.5 levels. Following the programme’s abrupt closure last year, she said, 97 per cent of reference-grade monitors disappeared in countries prioritised by the EPIC Air Quality Fund. She added that a study found pollution levels subsequently increased. “Someone else’s monitors operate on someone else’s priorities. Air quality infrastructure persists when it’s owned by the country that’s breathing the air,” she said. Established in 2024, the EPIC Air Quality Fund now supports 70 awardees in 44 countries, providing grants of between US$50,000 and US$75,000 over 18 months. Hasenkopf said the fund had recorded an 80 per cent increase in open air quality monitoring data in Africa during its first 18 months, alongside 16 national policy impacts. She cited The Gambia as an example of how locally generated data could influence policy. The country, which she said had no air quality monitoring three years ago, now has data that helped inform the drafting of its first air quality standards. The data was collected by a pulmonologist and a colleague, and the standards have since been passed by Parliament, she said. In Honduras, Sustenta Honduras Communications Lead Baleria Savion said the organisation had expanded air quality monitoring from two major cities to more than 60 locations across the country. She said the EPIC Air Quality Fund had ranked Honduras third among 147 countries for air quality data gaps in 2023. “Air quality is actually the leading cause of death in our country and it reduces life expectancy by two and a half years,” Savion said. “Before we only had monitors in two of the main cities, but now we have more than 60 across the territory.” She said national media outlets had begun using data from the network because it was the only available source of information on air quality in several areas. Savion added that a member of Congress had pledged to introduce an air quality law, which the organisation hopes will be achieved by 2027. Clean Energy Nepal Programme Coordinator Prakash Lama said the country’s annual average PM2.5 concentration had been reported at 51.7 micrograms per cubic metre, approximately 10 times the World Health Organization’s recommended guideline. He cited a government study that attributed about 42,000 deaths to air pollution, including 26,000 premature deaths annually, and estimated the economic cost at more than six per cent of Nepal’s gross domestic product. Lama said the challenge extended beyond the absence of policies or monitoring infrastructure to the availability and continuity of reliable data. His organisation has deployed 20 sensors across 10 cities to complement government monitoring and submitted recommendations on Nepal’s proposed national PM2.5 standard. He called for dedicated climate financing for air quality initiatives, warning that the issue should not remain an underfunded development priority. Deo Okure, Head of Research and Global Partnerships at AirQo and co-facilitator of the Africa Clean Air Network (AfriCAN), said the organisation operates more than 600 monitors across over 16 African cities. He estimated that Africa has about 2,000 active air quality monitors, compared with approximately 10,000 active reference stations in the United States. Okure questioned the extent to which funding commitments announced at successive climate summits translate into resources for communities and countries most affected by pollution. “Almost every COP brings some sort of funding commitments but … very little of that translates into what you would see that could catalyze action at local levels or in … countries that are most affected,” he said. He also cautioned against treating open air quality data as cost-free, pointing out that monitoring infrastructure, data collection and analysis require sustained investment. “When you say open data it doesn’t mean free data. Someone has paid for it,” he said. Okure urged funders to support less visible but essential areas of the work, including technical and institutional capacity development. Teddy Nabakooza Galiwango, Principal Environmental Officer of Uganda’s Kingdom of Buganda, said investment in monitoring should be accompanied by efforts to ensure that data informs practical interventions. “Expansion of data monitoring, but as we do that, it’s important to strengthen the pathway from data to action,” she said. Savion proposed a minimum target for the next year, urging stakeholders to ensure that every country has at least one air quality monitor providing publicly accessible data. “By next year we should make sure all countries have at least one air quality monitor that provides open access to that data,” she said.

items.title: PTA finalises licensing framework for 'sky-high' internet, telecommunication services
items.description: The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) said on Tuesday that it had finalised a licensing framework for satellite-based in-flight telecommunication services, “paving way for internet connectivity and other digital services aboard aircraft”. “Under the framework, licensed in-flight telecommunication services providers would be able to use satellites to offer connectivity to Pakistani-registered aircraft, subject to registration with the Pakistan Space Activities Regulatory Board and compliance with PTA’s licensing requirements,” the authority said in a press release on Tuesday. It added that transit aircraft passing through Pakistani airspace would require a no-objection certificate from the authority, subject to applicable compliance requirements. It said that the introduction of in-flight telecommunication services would “enhance passenger experience through seamless in-flight internet connectivity, enabling access to digital services, entertainment, personal communication and work-related activities”. It added that the initiative would further strengthen the authority’s efforts to expand digital connectivity in Pakistan by “extending telecommunication services beyond terrestrial networks and enabling seamless connectivity during air travel”.

items.title: Kozah / Cour d’appel de Kara : 40 dossiers inscrits au rôle de la session d’assises 2026
items.description: Kara, 17 nov. (ATOP) – La Cour d’appel de Kara a ouvert, le lundi 16 novembre à Kara, sa session d’assises de l’année judiciaire 2026. Au total, 40 dossiers impliquant 57 accusés sont inscrits au rôle de cette session, consacrée au jugement des affaires criminelles et à la manifestation de la vérité judiciaire. Placée sous le signe de la rigueur et de l’efficacité, cette session qui se poursuivra jusqu’au 11 décembre prochain, traduit la volonté des autorités judiciaires de renforcer la lutte contre l’impunité et de garantir la sécurité des citoyens. Elle s’inscrit dans la dynamique impulsée par le garde des Sceaux, ministre de la Justice et des Droits de l’Homme, autour d’une justice plus ferme, plus humaine et plus rapide. L’examen des 40 dossiers, qui concernent 57 accusés, dont la plupart sont en détention préventive, met en évidence plusieurs préoccupations liées à la criminalité et à la cohésion sociale. Les crimes contre la vie occupent une majeure place avec 16 dossiers portant notamment sur des assassinats, des meurtres, des coups mortels et des parricides. Selon les éléments d’instruction, ces actes trouvent souvent leur origine dans des facteurs tels que la consommation d’alcool, la jalousie et les conflits fonciers ou familiaux. Les atteintes à la dignité humaine et à l’intégrité des personnes constituent également une part importante des affaires qui seront examinées. Dix-sept dossiers concernent les viols et les actes de pédophilie. Face à la gravité de ces faits, le ministère public entend faire preuve d’une grande fermeté dans ses réquisitions. La session porte également sur des formes de criminalité plus complexes, notamment les vols aggravés, les enlèvements avec demande de rançon, la traite des personnes, les faits d’empoisonnement et les détournements de deniers publics. Le président de la Cour d’appel de Kara, Kutuhun Kossi, a souligné la portée particulière de cette session, qu’il inscrit dans le contexte de la refondation institutionnelle du pays. Il a relevé qu’elle témoigne de l’attachement des plus hautes autorités de l’Etat, à la primauté du droit et au respect des droits de l’Homme. Le président de la Cour a rappelé que, bien que prévue par la loi, la tenue des assises ne constitue pas une simple formalité judiciaire. Elle représente a-t-il précisé, un moment important où la justice se rend au nom du peuple, face aux atteintes les plus graves à la vie, à l’intégrité, à la dignité humaine et à la paix sociale. Le président Kutuhun a, par ailleurs, indiqué que les travaux se dérouleront dans le strict respect des principes fondamentaux de la justice, à savoir la présomption d’innocence, les droits de la défense et le principe du contradictoire, avec la garantie de l’assistance des avocats. Il a insisté sur la nécessité d’une recherche rigoureuse, sereine et impartiale de la vérité. Le président a enfin rappelé aux jurés et assesseurs la noblesse de leur mission, en tant que représentants de la voix du peuple togolais dans le processus judiciaire. ATOP/SG/TAL/BA

items.title: GreenFaith joins Make Polluters Pay coalition to honour Guterres for climate leadership
items.description: GreenFaith has joined the Make Polluters Pay International Coalition to honour United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres for his leadership in the global climate movement and his calls for the fossil fuel industry to be held accountable for the climate crisis. The recognition was presented during the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, in what is expected to be Mr Guterres’ final participation in the UN climate negotiations as Secretary-General. The award acknowledges his sustained advocacy for governments to accelerate the transition away from fossil fuels and ensure that companies responsible for climate damage contribute to addressing its impact. Representatives of the coalition, including GreenFaith Global Program Director Meryne Warah, Fill the Fund Global Convenor Harjeet Singh, and coalition convenors Louise Hutchins and David Hillman, presented the honour. At COP31, Mr Guterres renewed his criticism of the fossil fuel industry, declaring that “fossil fuels must go the way of the dinosaurs” and warning that industry lobbying was undermining efforts to address the climate crisis. He also called on governments to tax windfall profits made by fossil fuel companies and channel the proceeds towards helping vulnerable countries recover from climate-related damage. “Those who profit most from fossil fuels must help foot the bill for the damage they have caused,” he said. Mr Guterres cited figures showing that the world’s nine largest oil companies made $95 billion in profits in the last quarter alone, while the Loss and Damage Fund had received approximately $600 million. He argued that taxing these profits would provide resources to support countries facing the devastating effects of climate change. Speaking on the recognition, Ms Warah said climate justice required protecting lives, dignity and the future of communities affected by the climate crisis. She noted that people of faith and frontline communities across the world were demanding an end to the destruction caused by fossil fuels and accountability from those who had profited from the industry. “Guterres has used his platform to speak truth to power, challenge the influence of the fossil fuel industry and remind governments that climate action must be rooted in justice. We are delighted to recognise his contribution to this global struggle,” she said. Convenor of the Make Polluters Pay International Coalition, Louise Hutchins, said the UN Secretary-General had used his position to confront one of the world’s most powerful industries and strengthen calls for accountability. She said his advocacy had helped advance the global campaign for climate justice and efforts to ensure that communities bearing the greatest costs of the climate crisis receive support. Other organisations represented in the recognition included Fill the Fund, Stamp Out Poverty, 350.org, Greenpeace International and the Make Big Polluters Pay Alliance Australia. The groups called on governments to move beyond statements of commitment and introduce legally binding measures requiring major polluters to contribute to addressing climate-related damage. The recognition comes as climate justice organisations intensify calls for a fairer financing system that places greater responsibility on fossil fuel companies for the environmental damage associated with their operations.

items.title: Tony Elumelu mobilise les chefs d’entreprise africains et les capitaux d’investissement pour accélérer l’intégration régionale et la transformation économique.
items.description: Lagos, Nigeria | 17 Novembre 2026 Heirs Holdings jouera un rôle de premier plan lors du Sommet inaugural sur l’intégration et l’investissement en Afrique de l’Ouest (WAIIS 2026) Heirs Holdings, le groupe d’investissement panafricain fondé par l’investisseur et philanthrope africain Tony O. Elumelu, CFR, jouera un rôle de premier plan lors du premier Sommet sur l’intégration et l’investissement en Afrique de l’Ouest (West Africa Integration and Investment Summit – WAIIS 2026), qui se tiendra du 16 au 18 novembre en Sierra Leone. En tant que Partenaire principal du Sommet, le Groupe mettra à contribution ses hauts dirigeants, son expertise en matière d’investissement ainsi que sa vaste expérience opérationnelle dans des secteurs clés de l’économie africaine, afin de faire progresser le programme d’intégration régionale et d’investissement en Afrique de l’Ouest. Elumelu, Président du Conseil d’administration de Heirs Holdings et membre du Conseil consultatif du secteur privé du Sommet, pilote la mobilisation du secteur privé autour de cet événement, organisé sous le haut patronage de Son Excellence Julius Maada Bio, Président de la Sierra Leone. Il sera accompagné de hauts responsables des différentes sociétés du portefeuille du Groupe, notamment Obong Idiong, Directeur général de Heirs Technologies, qui interviendra lors de la session consacrée aux opportunités d’investissement. Il abordera notamment la question de la connexion des marchés ouest-africains à travers les systèmes de paiement, les données et les réseaux numériques. Peter Ikenga, Directeur général de Transcorp Power, coprésidera quant à lui la session consacrée à l'énergie, aux côtés de Mamadou Sangafowa-Coulibaly, ministre des Mines, du Pétrole et de l'Énergie de Côte d'Ivoire. Le Sommet réunira des chefs d'État africains, des décideurs politiques, des investisseurs institutionnels, des institutions de financement du développement ainsi que des chefs d'entreprise, dans le but d'accélérer l'intégration économique et de libérer le potentiel des opportunités d'investissement en Afrique de l'Ouest. Fervent défenseur de l' Africapitalisme , M. Elumelu, expert en redressement d'entreprises, promeut le principe selon lequel le développement de l'Afrique doit être porté par les entrepreneurs et les entreprises africains, grâce à des investissements privés à long terme générateurs de richesses économiques et sociales. Son engagement à la tête de cette initiative au WAIIS traduit sa conviction selon laquelle l'intégration régionale doit aller au-delà des engagements politiques pour se concrétiser à travers des partenariats commerciaux opérationnels, des investissements transfrontaliers et le développement d'entreprises africaines compétitives. Le rôle majeur de Heirs Holdings au WAIIS repose également sur son envergure, l'étendue de son empreinte en matière d'investissement et son expérience avérée dans la création et le développement d'entreprises dans des secteurs essentiels à la transformation économique de l'Afrique. Au 31 mars 2026, la valeur des sociétés composant son portefeuille s'élevait à environ 15,08 milliards de dollars américains . Avec des investissements et des activités opérationnelles dans 24 pays, ainsi qu'un effectif de plus de 40 000 collaborateurs au sein du Groupe et de ses sociétés en portefeuille, Heirs Holdings constitue une importante plateforme panafricaine d'investissement du secteur privé. Pour Heirs Holdings, l'intégration de l'Afrique de l'Ouest représente une opportunité majeure de renforcer le potentiel économique de la région et son attractivité auprès des investisseurs. Une région davantage interconnectée permet de créer des marchés plus vastes, de renforcer les échanges commerciaux intrarégionaux, de faciliter la circulation des capitaux, d'attirer les investissements, de créer des emplois et de permettre aux entreprises africaines de changer d'échelle et de rivaliser plus efficacement sur le marché mondial. Alors que les gouvernements, les investisseurs et les chefs d'entreprise se réunissent en Sierra Leone, Heirs Holdings réaffirme son engagement à collaborer avec les partenaires des secteurs public et privé afin de transformer l'intégration régionale en une réalité économique et commerciale concrète, créatrice de valeur économique et sociale durable à travers le continent. À propos de Heirs Holdings Heirs Holdings est une société d'investissement panafricaine de premier plan. Son portefeuille d'investissements couvre les secteurs de l'énergie, de l'électricité, de la banque, de l'assurance et des services financiers, des technologies, de l'immobilier, de l'hôtellerie et de la santé. Le Groupe exerce ses activités dans vingt-quatre pays à travers le monde. Heirs Holdings s'inspire du concept d' Africapitalisme , qui repose sur la conviction que le secteur privé constitue le principal moteur de la création de richesses économiques et sociales en Afrique. Guidé par cette philosophie, Heirs Holdings privilégie les investissements à long terme en mettant à la disposition des sociétés de son portefeuille des capitaux stratégiques, une expertise sectorielle, une expérience reconnue en matière de redressement et de transformation d'entreprises, ainsi qu'une excellence opérationnelle. L’article Tony Elumelu mobilise les chefs d’entreprise africains et les capitaux d’investissement pour accélérer l’intégration régionale et la transformation économique. est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .
