items.title: Vehicles without fitness, emission tests to be barred from Islamabad to curb smog
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The government on Tuesday decided to bar vehicles without fitness and emission testing from entering Islamabad, as part of measures to curb smog and air pollution in the capital. The decision was taken at a meeting chaired by Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry to review steps for smog prevention and reduction of air pollution. The meeting reviewed the current smog situation in Islamabad, the Air Quality Index (AQI) and ongoing measures to control air pollution. Chaudhry directed all relevant departments to ensure coordinated and effective measures to control air pollution and prevent smog. He said Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi was himself monitoring the entire process of anti-smog measures in Islamabad and their implementation. He contended that Islamabad’s AQI in October and November this year had remained better than the same period last year. According to data published by the Pakistan Environmental Protection Agency (Pak-EPA), the average AQI index for Islamabad was 148 this October , compared to an average of 169 in October 2025 . During the meeting, it was decided that heavy fines would be imposed on those involved in open burning and other smog-causing activities. Chaudhry warned of first information reports, arrests and heavy fines against violators of environmental laws. Strict action would also be taken against smoke-emitting brick kilns and industrial units, he added. The minister stressed that public cooperation was crucial for smog control and improvement in air quality, and citizens would have to play a responsible role. The additional deputy commissioner (ADC) (General), ADC (Revenue), the senior superintendent of police (Operations) and the chief traffic officer attended the meeting, alongside the Pak-EPA and excise directors and other relevant officials. In the past few years, air pollution has become one of the most pressing public health and environmental crises facing Pakistan. Various cities deal with smog, attributed mainly to industrial emissions, vehicular pollution , stubble burning and air movement . Last month, a two-day Pakistan National Clean Air Conference concluded with the adoption of the Islamabad Clean Air Compact, calling for coordinated federal and provincial action, stricter enforcement, regular emissions inventories and annual reviews to tackle air pollution. The National Assembly Standing Committee on Climate Change and Environmental Coordination has recommended the introduction of a regular vehicle emission testing mechanism in Islamabad and called for updating the Pakistan Environmental Protection Act, 1997, to bring it in line with current environmental challenges and international commitments. Last year, Pak-EPA launched large-scale inspections of vehicles and industrial units, while demolishing non-compliant brick kilns as part of a multi-tier plan to curb escalating air pollution.

items.title: Abu Jinapor questions NDC’s consistency over US$60.68m presidential jet
items.description: Former Lands and Natural Resources Minister Samuel Abu Jinapor has questioned the government’s decision to acquire a US$60.68 million presidential aircraft, accusing the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) of abandoning its earlier position on such expenditure. The Damongo MP says the acquisition of a new Falcon 6X executive jet raises questions about the party’s consistency, particularly given its opposition to proposals for a new presidential aircraft when it was in opposition. The Ghana Air Force took delivery of the French-manufactured aircraft on Monday, November 16, 2026, following parliamentary approval of the purchase in December 2025. In a Facebook post on Tuesday, November 17, Mr Abu Jinapor recalled that during parliamentary consideration of the 2026 Budget, the Minority raised concerns about the government’s plans to acquire presidential aircraft. He said the Majority disputed the Minority’s characterisation of the proposed expenditure and sought to justify the acquisition. According to him, it was suggested during the debate that the procurement and delivery process would take several years, creating the impression that the aircraft would not be delivered during President John Mahama’s tenure. He questioned how the aircraft had arrived barely a year later. “Yet, yesterday, barely a year later, the aircraft has been delivered. How does the government explain this remarkable turn of events?” he asked. Mr Abu Jinapor also recalled that leading NDC figures had opposed proposals to acquire a new presidential jet while the party was in opposition, arguing that the country’s economic circumstances did not justify such expenditure and that public resources should instead be directed towards improving the welfare of ordinary Ghanaians. “What has changed?” he asked. He argued that the acquisition required justification at a time when many Ghanaians continued to grapple with the cost of living and youth unemployment remained a concern. He also questioned the government’s decision to commit such resources to the aircraft while its flagship 24-hour economy programme was yet to deliver the transformation promised to Ghanaians. “The question is not simply whether Ghana requires a safe and reliable presidential aircraft. It is whether those who condemned such expenditure when they were in opposition can now defend it without adequately explaining what has changed,” he stated. He maintained that a position considered unacceptable when the NDC was in opposition should not become acceptable simply because the party was now in government. Minority demands full disclosure Mr Abu Jinapor said the Minority Caucus on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration Committee would demand full disclosure and accountability from the government over the acquisition. He said the caucus would pursue the matter in Parliament and seek answers on the total cost to the taxpayer, the financing arrangements, the procurement and approval processes, and the justification for acquiring the aircraft at this time. The Minority would also demand the full documentation relating to the transaction. Mr Abu Jinapor insisted that public expenditure of such magnitude required transparency, accountability and rigorous parliamentary scrutiny. He said the government must account to Parliament and the Ghanaian public for every dollar committed to the purchase. “Public expenditure of this magnitude demands transparency, accountability and rigorous parliamentary scrutiny,” he said. He called for greater consistency in public life, insisting that political office should not become a reason for abandoning previously held positions.

items.title: One dead, tanker driver critically injured in fire outbreak at Amamprobi Junction
items.description: One person has died, while a fuel tanker driver has sustained serious injuries following an accident that triggered a fire outbreak at Amamprobi Junction on the Mamfe–Adawso road in the Eastern Region. The deceased, identified as the tanker’s mate, was reportedly burnt beyond recognition after the vehicle caught fire. The accident involved a fuel tanker and a Kia Rhino truck with registration number GN 5021 2016. The tanker driver also sustained serious injuries and is said to be in critical condition. Personnel of the Ghana National Fire Service were dispatched to the scene to contain the fire. Following the incident, the Eastern Regional Fire Command has advised motorists and other road users to avoid the affected stretch until the situation is brought under control. The Command’s Regional Public Relations Officer, DOIII Ohemeng Aaron, urged motorists to use the Adukrom route as an alternative. He also appealed to commuters and other travellers to stay away from the accident scene and exercise caution to protect themselves.

items.title: ‘Nigeria is finished’ narrative costing economy investments, jobs — FG
items.description: By John Alechenu, Abuja The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has said Nigeria is paying a heavy economic price for negative narratives, misinformation and damaging perceptions about the country. Negative stories, he said, are not merely public relations problems. They discourage investors, constrain businesses, and drive away skilled talent. Oyedele spoke at the ongoing 2026 World Public Relations Forum (WPRF) in Abuja on Tuesday. He identified public trust as a critical factor in attracting investment, sustaining businesses and securing citizens’ support for government policies. According to him, trust is the currency that underpins economic activities and determines whether citizens cooperate with government, investors commit capital and businesses expand. Oyedele said, “Trust is the one currency that sits beneath all the other currencies. When trust is strong, citizens cooperate, capital flows, businesses invest, and reforms get a fair hearing. When trust is weak, even sound policies meet suspicion, and every explanation sounds like an excuse.” The minister said the economic consequences of negative narratives are often overlooked. The country could lose investments and valuable human capital when its public image was dominated by stories of failure and hopelessness. He cited damaging perceptions expressed in phrases such as “Nigeria is finished”, “Nigeria is a scam”, and “Nigeria happened to me”, warning that such narratives could influence investment decisions and undermine confidence in the country’s economic prospects. Oyedele further explained that the cost went beyond reputational damage. Investors demand higher returns to compensate for perceived risks, businesses postpone expansion plans, and talented Nigerians seek opportunities elsewhere. He, however, acknowledged that citizens have the right to expose government failures, demand accountability and draw attention to the difficulties they faced. Responsible communication, he insisted, must not be confused with suppressing criticism. The country’s story must reflect both its challenges and progress, he added. Government and businesses could not rely on publicity to conceal poor performance or substitute communication for service delivery. “We cannot communicate our way out of conflicts,” he said. Oyedele stressed that public communication must be backed by measurable results. Citizens judged government not by announcements or budgetary provisions but by what they experienced. The minister noted that the disconnect between government claims and citizens’ everyday experiences had contributed to distrust, making it difficult for even well-intentioned policies to gain public acceptance. He used the public’s response to declining inflation figures to illustrate the challenge. Although the October 2026 inflation rate was reported at 14.06 per cent, the lowest in six years, many Nigerians remain unconvinced because prices of essential commodities such as bread and milk were still high. Oyedele equally explained that a decline in inflation did not mean prices were falling but that the rate at which prices increased was slowing down. Failure to explain that distinction, he said, could deepen frustration and create expectations that further influence market behaviour. In the controversy surrounding the government’s tax reforms, Oyedele said misinformation had distorted the intention and benefits of the measures, including provisions designed to protect small businesses and exempt low-income earners. Some of the people the reforms were intended to benefit had opposed them because of misleading information, he said, underscoring the need for clear and sustained public engagement. “Facts do not defend themselves,” he said, adding that “in a contest between a careful explanation and a frightening headline, the headline wins.” The minister also expressed concern about social media platforms, where sensational and divisive content often attracts more attention than factual corrections. “Outrage pays, correction does not,” he said. He warned that the growing use of artificial intelligence had made the spread of misinformation more dangerous, as convincing images, voices and documents could now be fabricated and circulated rapidly. Oyedele urged public relations and communication professionals to become involved in policy formulation from the beginning rather than being brought in only when government or businesses faced communication crises. He challenged media organisations, influencers and other information gatekeepers to take greater responsibility for the content they circulate. “Verify before you amplify. Correct as loudly as you reported when you make mistakes. Hold good news and bad news to the same standard of proof,” he urged. He also called on government institutions and businesses to make policy and economic information accessible, respond to public complaints and measure the effectiveness of their communication by whether people understood the message and could see the results. Oyedele maintained that the credibility of any national or corporate narrative ultimately depended on the lived experiences of the people, not the volume of publicity deployed to promote it. “Experiencing is knowing,” he said. The post ‘Nigeria is finished’ narrative costing economy investments, jobs — FG appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ohene Kwame Frimpong agrees to extradition from the Netherlands to face US charges – Lawyer
items.description: The detained Member of Parliament for Asante Akim North, Ohene Kwame Frimpong, has agreed not to challenge his extradition from the Netherlands to the United States, a member of his legal team, Elvis Adu-Ameyaw, has said. Mr Adu-Ameyaw said the MP had decided to consent to the extradition to allow the allegations against him to be resolved. Ahead of the extradition hearing scheduled for Wednesday, November 18, 2026, the lawyer said his client was concerned about the plight of his constituents and Ghanaians generally. “Honourable Ohene Kwame Frimpong is concerned about the plight of his people. I am referring to the people of Asante Akim North and the Ghanaian people at large,” he said. Mr Adu-Ameyaw said the MP would not contest the legal basis of the extradition request when the case is heard in an Amsterdam court. “What that means is that we are not going to challenge the legal basis of his extradition to the United States of America tomorrow in court,” he stated. He added that the court had already been informed of Mr Frimpong’s position. The lawyer said his client wanted to be physically present in the United States to work with his legal team towards resolving the allegations against him. “He took that bold step or that decision because he wants to see the final resolution of these allegations, and for him to be able to do that, there is a need for him to be present in the United States to work with his lawyers towards resolving these issues,” he said. He spoke on Starr FM. Mr Frimpong was arrested at Amsterdam’s Schiphol Airport on May 10, 2026, after arriving from Ghana. His arrest followed an extradition request from the United States linked to allegations of romance scams and money laundering. He has remained in Dutch custody after an initial bail application and a subsequent appeal were unsuccessful. Majority Chief Whip in Parliament, Rockson-Nelson Dafeamekpor, had earlier disclosed that the extradition hearing was scheduled for November 18. Parliament has also engaged Ghana’s diplomatic mission in The Hague over the matter, while Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa has confirmed that consular assistance has been provided to the detained MP. The Amsterdam court is expected to consider the extradition proceedings on Wednesday, November 18, 2026. Mr Frimpong has not been convicted of the offences alleged against him. His decision not to challenge the extradition request does not, by itself, amount to a determination of the criminal allegations.

L'operatrice economique Bassira Kouma, originaire de la ville, a offert 25 tonnes de riz, soit 1 000 sacs de 25 kilos, aux populations vulnerables. Parmi les beneficiaires figurent des personnes deplacees internes, des familles d'accueil, des personnes vivant avec un handicap et des femmes cheffes de famille. Le don a ete remis en presence du prefet du cercle et des forces vives, dans le cadre du Mois de la solidarite. items.title: Warri community threatens economic shutdown over INEC ward delineation
items.description: Ifie-kporo Community in Warri South Local Government Area has faulted the delineation report uploaded on the portal of the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC. The community demanded the inclusion of Ijala Ward, arguing that some areas allocated wards were not as large as theirs. Vice Chairman of Ifiekporo Community, Mr Jolomi Enonuya, in a statement, warned that the threat to cripple the country’s economy remained strong if the report was not revised. According to him, since the creation of Warri South Local Government Area in 1991, governments at all levels had refused to acknowledge the numerical growth and economic viability of Ifiekporo, Ajaetan, Ikeren and Utunwa. Enonuya reminded the Federal Government that oil facilities, including oil fields operated by Conoil and Seplat, petroleum depots belonging to Matrix Energy Ltd, AYM Shafa, Pinnacle Oil and Gas, Parker Oil, A & E Petrol, and Keonamex Oil and Gas, as well as the Warri Refining and Petrochemical Company (WRPC), were located in their communities. He said: “What is the rationale behind INEC uploading three wards for the riverbank of Warri GRA, a marketplace where people come to do business and return to their respective homes in Ogbe-Ijoh and neighbouring LGAs, but not doing the same for Ijala (comprising Ifie, Ajaetan, Ikeren and Utunwa)? “It is with a great sense of anger and utter displeasure that I call on President Bola Tinubu and INEC to immediately address the lopsided units and wards uploaded on INEC’s portal as they relate to Warri South Local Government Area. “Since the creation of this LGA in 1991, the government and leaders of Warri South have refused to acknowledge our numerical growth and economic viability, which are what have conferred oil-producing status on this LGA. “This Ijala axis of the Warri Islands has four communities and hosts oil companies, including the Warri Refinery. It also has arable lands, which are the mainstay of Warri South today. “The demand for the creation of Ijala Ward from the existing Obodo/Omadino Ward is legitimate because we have the numerical and economic strength to become a stand-alone ward. “For clarity, Obodo and Omadino are two autonomous communities in Warri South. The other communities are Ifie, Ajaetan, Ikeren, Utunwa, Ubeji, Egbokodo, Orere-Uluba, Ubiro, Aja-Osolo, Uwakeno, Ugboritseduwa, Ubarira, Ugbikoko and Jaluwa-Efueye. “When the Supreme Court-ordered ward delineation commenced in 2023, INEC officials visited our communities to carry out their fieldwork. “But to our greatest disappointment, in all the proposals INEC shared with ethnic stakeholders, not a single ward was proposed for us. Frustratingly, we are still pegged back in Obodo/Omadino Ward. “Is INEC telling us that we have not increased numerically since 1991? Is INEC telling us that only those with dollars and violent tendencies are fit to be allotted wards? “Allotting Ijala Ward to us based on what INEC uploaded on its portal is non-negotiable, and it is now or never. Otherwise, we will speak the only language the Federal Government understands – crippling the economy.” The post Warri community threatens economic shutdown over INEC ward delineation appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Sudan: New Fonj Region establishes new rules of engagement on ground following “Violations”
items.description: Developments on the ground continue to unfold in Sudan’s war, which has been raging since mid-April between the army based in Port Sudan and the Sudan Founding Alliance Forces (TASIS), amid ongoing shifts in military confrontations. The United Nations has warned that the conflict in Sudan continues to deepen civilian suffering, three and a half years after its outbreak. Shifting front lines are forcing increasing numbers of families to flee, leaving many homeless amid a severe funding shortfall. It also noted that Sudanese nationals have become the largest nationality among those arriving in Europe via the Eastern Mediterranean route, as a result of the continuing conflict, while the army has rejected all initiatives aimed at ending the war. Meanwhile, on the military front, Sudan Mix reported that TASIS forces had established full control over the areas of Mayful and Jabal Al-Tin, located in Bau County in the south of the Blue Nile Region (New Fonj Region), following military confrontations in the area during the early hours and morning of Saturday. In an official statement, the forces said they had achieved “significant victories in the Blue Nile Region/New Fonj on Saturday, liberating the areas of Jabal Al-Tin, Qamberi and Mabingo, which fall under Bau County in the Blue Nile Region/New Fonj. Their forces also dealt a crushing blow to the terrorist Muslim Brotherhood militia during decisive battles.” They affirmed that they were continuing their “steady advance to clear the remaining areas, amid a state of collapse within the ranks of the terrorist militias, foreign mercenaries and mercenary groups.” The statement continued: “The heroes of our forces delivered lessons in courage and bravery during today’s battles, inflicting heavy losses on the enemy in personnel and equipment. Large numbers of its members were killed or captured, while the remnants of its forces fled, leaving behind quantities of weapons and military equipment. Our forces thus established full control over these strategic areas in the region.” The forces also affirmed their “steadfast commitment to protecting civilians in the liberated areas, working to secure their safety and ensure the delivery of assistance after freeing them from the oppression of extremist groups. They also reassure residents that their safety remains an absolute priority and urge them to stay away from areas of military operations to protect their lives.” The Bleeding Region This shift on the ground comes in the wake of grave violations in the region, one of Sudan’s richest areas, located approximately 160 kilometres from Ethiopia’s Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam, allegedly perpetrated by the army affiliated with the Port Sudan authorities and the Islamist militias allied with it. In July 2026, an army-operated drone targeted a gathering of displaced people in the Qoz Al-Duhaish area, at the Al-Mughira team site in the Southern Badia of Al-Tadamon locality, in the New Fonj Region. The attack killed and injured dozens of civilians, according to documentation by Sudanese reports and local organisations. Reports confirm that the region, rich in gold, silver, copper, chromium and magnesium, has been subjected to sustained aerial bombardment throughout the war, causing extensive destruction to healthcare and educational facilities. Food insecurity has also intensified as most agricultural and pastoral activities have ground to a halt, following the bombing of the United Nations World Food Programme office in the area in May 2025. Earlier, the United Federal Party accused the Sudanese army, led by Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, and the extremist groups allied with it of committing “fully fledged war crimes” in the New Fonj Region. It described a series of systematic attacks targeting civilians, markets, hospitals and water sources over recent months, warning that the continuation of these violations threatened to turn Sudan into an “open arena for revenge and systematic destruction.” In a strongly worded statement issued on Tuesday, 19 May 2026, the party said that “the areas of Yabus, Shali Al-Fil, Balila, Anili and Al-Layli have been subjected to repeated bombardment by army-operated drones, resulting in dozens of civilian casualties and widespread destruction of the social and service infrastructure, as well as the essential resources of daily life.” The statement pointed out that “Yabus Hospital was completely burned down, alongside the destruction of citizens’ homes and the targeting of markets, mills and drinking-water sources. It stressed that the bombardment directly struck popular markets and civilian facilities, including Shali Al-Fil Market, where a pregnant woman was killed in an attack, in addition to the destruction of a commercial vehicle and service facilities in Balila.” The party added that “the bombardment of the Anili area resulted in the killing of seven citizens and the injury of large numbers of civilians, most of them women and children. Meanwhile, repeated attacks on Balila Market on 2 May left more than 14 people dead and eight wounded, while water sources and commercial shops sustained extensive destruction.” A New Beginning According to reports, more than half a million people live in the Fonj Region in huts built from locally available materials, lacking even the most basic necessities of life, including healthcare and education. The region has endured decades of neglect and a lack of essential services. Meanwhile, more than 400,000 residents face the threat of food insecurity, despite living in one of Sudan’s most fertile areas, which also receives some of the country’s heaviest rainfall. A report issued by the Sudanese Doctors for Development Organisation confirmed that the region was subjected to more than 40 airstrikes between March and September 2025, targeting residential areas as well as healthcare and educational facilities, resulting in significant losses of life and property. The takeover of the region by the Sudan Founding Alliance Forces (TASIS) could usher in a transformation, given that it lies at the heart of a strategic triangle linking Sudan’s Blue Nile State, the borders of Ethiopia’s Sixth Region, and South Sudan’s Upper Nile State. Like other parts of Sudan, the region has suffered the consequences of Muslim Brotherhood rule. Observers maintain that, nearly 34 years after the Brotherhood came to power, the outcome of the coup that claimed to pursue reform has proven to be an ever-deepening deterioration across every aspect of the country. This decline reached its peak with the secession of South Sudan, the proliferation of armed militias loyal to Islamists, and the country’s descent into international isolation and economic blockade. Observers argue that “the Muslim Brotherhood’s project in Sudan was not founded on creating a democratic experience, nor even on repairing the political situation at the time. Rather, it was built on the idea of seizing power and then moving to a stage of consolidating control over it and refusing to relinquish it. This practice was carried out in the name of the Islamic Movement, reflecting the movement’s narrow conception of the state and its lack of belief in democracy.” Following the outbreak of the ongoing war, the organisation worked relentlessly to obstruct efforts to secure a truce in Sudan and derail negotiations aimed at ending the conflict, capitalising on its influence within the Sudanese army and its military and media role in the conflict. Having been ousted in the December Revolution, the group does not want the Sudanese state to achieve stability, nor does it regard the establishment of peace and an end to the war as serving its political project, amid the official protection afforded by army commander Abdel Fattah al-Burhan.

items.title: ‘Yankee Go Home’
items.description: Introduction by Sophia Grace Carter I n September , the photojournalist Lynsey Addario traveled to Venezuela with Atlantic staff writer Anne Applebaum. They arrived in a country devastated by back-to-back earthquakes in June and still reeling from the U.S. military operation that had toppled its president, Nicolás Maduro, in January. Drawing on her reporting there, Applebaum argues in The Atlantic ’s December issue that the Trump administration has revived a familiar form of Yankee imperialism, laying claim to Venezuela’s oil troves with little regard for the interests of its people. Addario’s images capture the head-spinning transformations under way—and how some citizens are chafing against the new political order and others are attempting to preserve some semblance of normalcy. [ From the December 2026 issue: Anne Applebaum on what the U.S. is really doing in Venezuela ] Addario has covered nearly every major global conflict of the past two decades—the U.S. invasions of Afghanistan and Iraq, the genocide in Darfur, the civil wars in Libya and Syria, Russia’s incursion into Ukraine. But she began her career in Latin America at 21, traveling through the region with her camera. In 2002, she documented the aftermath of a failed coup attempt against the regime of Hugo Chávez, Maduro’s predecessor, and, in 2024, for this magazine, she photographed a group of migrants crossing the Darién Gap , many of them Venezuelan. Nearly 8 million Venezuelans—about 25 percent of the population —have fled the country over the past decade. On this year’s trip, she witnessed the circumstances that have driven that exodus. Once the richest country in South America, Venezuela now suffers from the world’s highest inflation rate, driven by a quarter century of political fracturing, corruption, economic mismanagement, and U.S. sanctions. Though the country possesses the world’s largest proven oil reserves—more than 300 billion barrels—electricity shortages are a fact of life, and many Venezuelans live in poverty amid crumbling infrastructure. When the earthquakes struck in June, the government’s ineffectual response left citizens to fend for themselves. The tremors killed at least 6,500 people; injured more than 16,800; and left about 17,000 homeless. In La Guaira, the city hardest hit, government rescue workers didn’t show up for days, so residents and volunteers mobilized to deliver aid on their own, turning schools into makeshift shelters and opening soup kitchens. Heeding the war photographer Robert Capa’s dictum that “If your pictures aren’t good enough, you’re not close enough,” Addario often spends time talking with her subjects before photographing them, trying to understand their life and circumstances. These conversations can be fraught, and Addario told me that she sometimes becomes the target of her subjects’ anger and frustration. But she can also serve as an outlet for them. In La Guaira, where she encountered people digging through the wreckage with their bare hands in search of the bodies of the missing, she sensed that some were grateful to have their loss memorialized. Months had passed, and they were still there searching. By photographing them, Addario hoped she might help ensure that “they don’t feel like it’s all been forgotten.” — Sophia Grace Carter Lynsey Addario for The Atlantic Jeanpier Bolívar, 34, and Juan José Meléndez, 27, pull in a nearly empty fishing net on Lake Maracaibo, a brackish estuary where oil extraction began more than a century ago. The lake is South America’s largest body of water—and its largest environmental disaster. Local fishermen say their catches have dwindled as pollution has worsened, and some resort to rinsing their crabs and shrimp with gasoline to remove the crude oil. Lynsey Addario for The Atlantic A thick sheen of petroleum coats the lake’s surface. More than two decades of neglect have left its waters poisoned by leaks and spills, and dotted with ghostly drilling platforms. Lynsey Addario for The Atlantic The oil industry has generated enormous wealth, even as many of the people living in the shadow of its pumps and refineries remain mired in poverty. Lynsey Addario for The Atlantic Residents gather on a street in the city of Maracaibo during a rolling blackout. Though Venezuela has the world’s largest proven oil reserves, the country’s deteriorating electrical grid causes regular power outages lasting six to eight hours. Lynsey Addario for The Atlantic A street market in Maracaibo in September. Skyrocketing inflation has driven up the cost of basic goods; prices sometimes change from one day to the next. Lynsey Addario for The Atlantic Venezuelans ride on public transportation in La Vega. The neighborhood was once a stronghold of Hugo Chávez, who ruled Venezuela from 1999 until his death in 2013. Lynsey Addario for The Atlantic A boy plays in an alley in La Vega. Lynsey Addario for The Atlantic Venezuelans were still searching for the bodies of loved ones amid mountains of brick and concrete in La Guaira in September, more than two months after back-to-back earthquakes devastated the region. Lynsey Addario for The Atlantic Women pray during an open-air Mass at the Basílica de Santa Teresa in Caracas. The church was damaged by the June earthquakes and declared unsafe to enter. Lynsey Addario for The Atlantic Venezuelan security forces barricade streets leading to Miraflores, the presidential palace in Caracas, as protesters demand the release of political prisoners. More than 320 remained incarcerated as of late October. Lynsey Addario for The Atlantic A woman dressed as the Statue of Liberty bound in chains faces a line of Venezuelan security forces during a demonstration in Caracas. Lynsey Addario for The Atlantic Anti-American graffiti in Caracas evokes decades of tension between Venezuela and the United States, even as Washington exerts growing influence over the country’s pliant interim government.

items.title: British Airways plane bound for Lagos veers off runway
items.description: By Dickson Omobola British Airways Flight BA75 from Heathrow, London, to Lagos, Nigeria, veered off the runway shortly before take-off today. The aircraft, which had up to 215 passengers on board, was subsequently grounded, resulting in the cancellation of the flight. Pictures shared with The Sun showed the Boeing 787 Dreamliner stranded, with its nose wheel stuck in a grass verge. According to The Sun, emergency services raced to the scene of the stranded aircraft, which had sparked disruption at the airport. Airport sources suggested to The Sun that pilot error could have been responsible for the incident, which occurred at about 10.40am. A source told The Sun, “The packed plane was all set to go and had pushed back from its stand, taxiing to the runway for take-off to Lagos. “Bafflingly, the plane appears to have simply been driven off the tarmac onto a grass verge. It is hard to understand what could be to blame for this, other than a most basic pilot error. “There are red faces all around the airline, and a hefty task clearing up the mess and looking after hundreds of disgruntled passengers who were strapped in their seats for lift-off.” British Airways told The Sun, “We are very sorry to our customers for the disruption to their flight. Our teams are working to get them on their way as quickly as possible and are in touch with them to put things right.” The post British Airways plane bound for Lagos veers off runway appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Les dirigeants de Heirs Holdings au cœur des échanges sur l’investissement lors du WAIIS 2026
items.description: Tony Elumelu mobilise les chefs d’entreprise africains et les capitaux d’investissement pour accélérer l’intégration régionale et la transformation économique. Lagos, Nigeria | 17 Novembre 2026 Heirs Holdings jouera un rôle de premier plan lors du Sommet inaugural sur l’intégration et l’investissement en Afrique de l’Ouest (WAIIS 2026) Heirs Holdings, le groupe d’investissement panafricain fondé par l’investisseur et philanthrope africain Tony O. Elumelu, CFR, jouera un rôle de premier plan lors du premier Sommet sur l’intégration et l’investissement en Afrique de l’Ouest (West Africa Integration and Investment Summit – WAIIS 2026), qui se tiendra du 16 au 18 novembre en Sierra Leone. En tant que Partenaire principal du Sommet, le Groupe mettra à contribution ses hauts dirigeants, son expertise en matière d’investissement ainsi que sa vaste expérience opérationnelle dans des secteurs clés de l’économie africaine, afin de faire progresser le programme d’intégration régionale et d’investissement en Afrique de l’Ouest. Elumelu, Président du Conseil d’administration de Heirs Holdings et membre du Conseil consultatif du secteur privé du Sommet, pilote la mobilisation du secteur privé autour de cet événement, organisé sous le haut patronage de Son Excellence Julius Maada Bio, Président de la Sierra Leone. Il sera accompagné de hauts responsables des différentes sociétés du portefeuille du Groupe, notamment Obong Idiong, Directeur général de Heirs Technologies, qui interviendra lors de la session consacrée aux opportunités d’investissement. Il abordera notamment la question de la connexion des marchés ouest-africains à travers les systèmes de paiement, les données et les réseaux numériques. Peter Ikenga, Directeur général de Transcorp Power, coprésidera quant à lui la session consacrée à l'énergie, aux côtés de Mamadou Sangafowa-Coulibaly, ministre des Mines, du Pétrole et de l'Énergie de Côte d'Ivoire. Le Sommet réunira des chefs d'État africains, des décideurs politiques, des investisseurs institutionnels, des institutions de financement du développement ainsi que des chefs d'entreprise, dans le but d'accélérer l'intégration économique et de libérer le potentiel des opportunités d'investissement en Afrique de l'Ouest. Fervent défenseur de l' Africapitalisme , M. Elumelu, expert en redressement d'entreprises, promeut le principe selon lequel le développement de l'Afrique doit être porté par les entrepreneurs et les entreprises africains, grâce à des investissements privés à long terme générateurs de richesses économiques et sociales. Son engagement à la tête de cette initiative au WAIIS traduit sa conviction selon laquelle l'intégration régionale doit aller au-delà des engagements politiques pour se concrétiser à travers des partenariats commerciaux opérationnels, des investissements transfrontaliers et le développement d'entreprises africaines compétitives. Le rôle majeur de Heirs Holdings au WAIIS repose également sur son envergure, l'étendue de son empreinte en matière d'investissement et son expérience avérée dans la création et le développement d'entreprises dans des secteurs essentiels à la transformation économique de l'Afrique. Au 31 mars 2026, la valeur des sociétés composant son portefeuille s'élevait à environ 15,08 milliards de dollars américains . Avec des investissements et des activités opérationnelles dans 24 pays, ainsi qu'un effectif de plus de 40 000 collaborateurs au sein du Groupe et de ses sociétés en portefeuille, Heirs Holdings constitue une importante plateforme panafricaine d'investissement du secteur privé. Pour Heirs Holdings, l'intégration de l'Afrique de l'Ouest représente une opportunité majeure de renforcer le potentiel économique de la région et son attractivité auprès des investisseurs. Une région davantage interconnectée permet de créer des marchés plus vastes, de renforcer les échanges commerciaux intrarégionaux, de faciliter la circulation des capitaux, d'attirer les investissements, de créer des emplois et de permettre aux entreprises africaines de changer d'échelle et de rivaliser plus efficacement sur le marché mondial. Alors que les gouvernements, les investisseurs et les chefs d'entreprise se réunissent en Sierra Leone, Heirs Holdings réaffirme son engagement à collaborer avec les partenaires des secteurs public et privé afin de transformer l'intégration régionale en une réalité économique et commerciale concrète, créatrice de valeur économique et sociale durable à travers le continent. À propos de Heirs Holdings Heirs Holdings est une société d'investissement panafricaine de premier plan. Son portefeuille d'investissements couvre les secteurs de l'énergie, de l'électricité, de la banque, de l'assurance et des services financiers, des technologies, de l'immobilier, de l'hôtellerie et de la santé. Le Groupe exerce ses activités dans vingt-quatre pays à travers le monde. Heirs Holdings s'inspire du concept d' Africapitalisme , qui repose sur la conviction que le secteur privé constitue le principal moteur de la création de richesses économiques et sociales en Afrique. Guidé par cette philosophie, Heirs Holdings privilégie les investissements à long terme en mettant à la disposition des sociétés de son portefeuille des capitaux stratégiques, une expertise sectorielle, une expérience reconnue en matière de redressement et de transformation d'entreprises, ainsi qu'une excellence opérationnelle. L’article Les dirigeants de Heirs Holdings au cœur des échanges sur l’investissement lors du WAIIS 2026 est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

Minority to demand procurement details of presidential jet purchase
items.description: The Minority in Parliament is demanding full disclosure of the procurement details surrounding the acquisition of a new presidential jet, following government’s announcement of the aircraft’s delivery. The Minority wants the government to present the contract, financing agreement and procurement approval to Parliament for scrutiny. Speaking on Joy FM’s Midday News on Tuesday, November 17, the Ranking Member on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, Samuel Abu Jinapor, said the Minority will pursue the matter in the House. According to him, government must explain the decision to acquire a new presidential jet, particularly given its previous opposition to such a purchase. He argued that the economic conditions the NDC government previously cited in opposing the purchase of a new presidential jet had not changed and had, in some cases, worsened. “We will take it up in Parliament. We want to ask for the details of this purchase, the procurement method used, the amount involved, the nature of this jet, and also press them to admit the issues of principle and admit that, as you said, if they’ve changed their mind, as you say, if it’s double standards, they should point it out,” he said. Read also: Ghana Air Force takes delivery of new Presidential Jet He also questioned the government’s justification for spending a reported GH¢720 million on the aircraft while struggling to meet certain financial obligations, including payments to the Judicial Service Staff Association of Ghana (JUSAG), nurses and teachers. The Ranking Member also rejected suggestions that the aircraft was being acquired for the Ghana Air Force rather than for presidential use. He explained that presidential aircraft have historically been housed with the Ghana Air Force, insisting that this does not change the purpose of the latest acquisition. “All presidential jets are housed with the Ghana Air Force. So they are trying to create the impression that some plane is being bought for the Ghana Air Force,” he said.

items.title: Ablakwa offers reward for information on Ghanaian woman allegedly assaulted in Iraq
items.description: Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa has announced a reward for anyone who provides credible information to help identify and locate a Ghanaian woman believed to have been assaulted by her employer in Iraq. The Minister is appealing to the public to assist ongoing efforts to investigate a viral video purportedly showing the woman being brutally assaulted. In a Facebook post shared on Tuesday, November 17, Mr Ablakwa urged anyone with relevant information about the incident to contact Ghana’s nearest diplomatic mission, assuring informants that a handsome reward awaits them. “Anyone with relevant information should contact our nearest embassy. A handsome reward awaits you,” he stated. He disclosed that Ghana’s diplomatic missions and partners in the Gulf region were working together to investigate the footage and establish the circumstances surrounding the alleged abuse. The investigation follows what the Minister described as a successful rescue operation in Iran, with the government now turning its attention to the disturbing video believed to have originated from neighbouring Iraq. “After our successful rescue operation in Iran, we are looking into that viral video supposedly emanating from Iraq, which shows a lady believed to be a Ghanaian being terribly assaulted by her boss,” he said. Mr Ablakwa assured Ghanaians that the government would pursue the matter and would not tolerate the abuse or mistreatment of its citizens outside the country. “No one will be allowed to mess around with a Ghanaian and get away with it,” he added.

items.title: Vinicius hits 12-minute hat-trick as Brazil thrash Singapore 7-0
items.description: Vinicius Junior hit a 12-minute hat-trick in the first half as Brazil turned on the style in a 7-0 trouncing of Singapore on Tuesday. Endrick, Estevao, Rayan and substitute Allan also scored as the South Americans brushed aside the hosts with a dominant performance at the National Stadium. Brazil were much changed from their 3-2 loss to Japan on Saturday in which manager Carlo Ancelotti and captain Raphinha were shown red cards, with Vinicius one of only four players retaining their places in the starting line-up. Bruno Guimaraes took over as skipper and set up the opener after nine minutes, playing a quick pass to Vinicius who wrong-footed Singapore captain Hariss Harun with his first touch before despatching a left-footed shot past goalkeeper Izwan Mahbud. The Real Madrid forward notched his second in the 15th minute after a quick counter-attack as Endrick laid the ball off for his unmarked team-mate to slot home. Vinicius was denied by Izwan shortly afterwards but he completed his hat-trick in the 21st minute when he was found unmarked in the six-yard box by Estevao’s low centre. Rayan had an effort disallowed for offside but Endrick added to Brazil’s lead in the 31st minute with a low effort from range which found the bottom right corner. Estevao also had a goal disallowed for a foul by Vinicius but the Chelsea winger added to Brazil’s tally just after the interval with a deflected shot from the edge of the box. Rayan rocked the crossbar soon after but the endeavour of the Bournemouth forward was rewarded in the 65th minute when he rounded substitute goalkeeper Syazwan Buhari to make it 6-0. Brazil rang the changes in the closing stages and Allan came off the bench to grab the seventh goal in the 74th minute. Speaking in the absence of the suspended Ancelotti, Brazil assistant Francesco Mauri lauded the commitment shown by Vinicius. “His attitude was fantastic. As we discussed before the match, you shouldn’t focus solely on the quality of the opponents, you just have to give your absolute best,” said the Italian. “He was a constant threat, providing great depth to our attack. He forced the opposition to double-mark him, which in turn allowed us to defend a bit more effectively.” Despite lengthy travel for the friendlies in Singapore, Mauri felt the effort had been worthwhile for the squad’s development. “Before the game, we told the players that it was really important to finish in the best way in these November FIFA dates because after this we have to wait until March for our next games, so it’s good to go home with a good feeling,” he said. items.title: Semaine mondiale de l’entrepreneuriat : les PME gabonaises réclament des marchés, pas des promesses
items.description: ‎‎Officiellement lancée ce mardi 17 novembre 2026 à la Baie des Rois, à Libreville, la Semaine mondiale de l’entrepreneuriat place les petites et moyennes entreprises au cœur des ambitions économiques du Gabon. Entre difficultés d’accès aux financements, marchés encore peu accessibles et formalisation, les entrepreneurs attendent désormais des actes. Un appel auquel le gouvernement entend répondre. ‎‎Photo de famille à l'issue de la cérémonie d'ouverture, le 17 novembre 2026 à Libreville. © GabonReview Les discours sont lancés, les attentes aussi. À l’occasion de l’ouverture officielle de la Semaine mondiale de l’entrepreneuriat, mardi 17 novembre 2026, à Libreville, les autorités et les représentants du secteur privé ont affiché une ambition commune : faire des PME gabonaises des acteurs à part entière de la transformation économique du pays. Placée sous le thème «Entreprendre au Gabon, produire au Gabon, réussir au Gabon» , cette édition entend surtout apporter des réponses aux difficultés qui freinent le développement des entreprises locales. ‎‎Pour la ministre des PME et des PMI chargée de l’entrepreneuriat, Zenaba Gninga Chaning, l’heure est à l’action. Elle a ainsi présenté six initiatives destinées à répondre aux préoccupations des entrepreneurs : le Pacte national pour le financement des PME, la grande rencontre entre PME et acheteurs, les journées de formalisation accélérée, le programme «PME gabonaises à l’heure du numérique», celui consacré à la production et à la transformation locale, ainsi que les assises des PME et pépinières de l’entrepreneuriat. «Nous voulons rapprocher les entrepreneurs des institutions financières, faciliter leur accès aux marchés, valoriser la production nationale», a-t-elle expliqué. Pour elle, cette mobilisation doit surtout trouver «une traduction concrète dans le quotidien de nos entreprises» . ‎ ‎L'entrepreneuriat, une véritable opportunité économique selon le vice-président du gouvernement Moments de l'évènement. © GabonReview ‎‎Un engagement que le vice-président du Gouvernement, Hermann Immongault, a également défendu, en appelant à la mobilisation de l’ensemble des acteurs économiques. Pour lui, le développement du Gabon ne saurait se construire sans des entreprises nationales fortes, compétitives et capables de créer de la richesse. «L’entrepreneuriat n’est plus une option. Il représente une véritable opportunité économique et, par voie de conséquence, un puissant levier de croissance durable» , a-t-il déclaré. Il a notamment interpellé les établissements bancaires et de microfinance sur les difficultés d’accès au crédit, tout en invitant les grandes entreprises à ouvrir davantage leurs marchés aux PME locales. ‎‎Mais derrière cette volonté affichée, les entrepreneurs attendent des changements tangibles. Prenant la parole, le représentant des PME, Théophane Moubebe Ndoume, est revenu sur les difficultés auxquelles ils font face, à savoir : l' accès au financement, insuffisance de fonds de roulement, référencement, délais de paiement et accès aux marchés. Sans réclamer de traitement de faveur, il a demandé aux pouvoirs publics et aux grandes entreprises de créer les conditions permettant aux PME de faire leurs preuves. «La PME gabonaise ne demande pas une économie de faveur. Elle demande une économie d’opportunité, de règles claires et de confiance» , a-t-il lancé. Il a surtout proposé la mise en place d’un mécanisme de suivi des engagements sur 30, 60 et 90 jours, afin d’évaluer les financements instruits, les commandes obtenues et les partenariats conclus. ‎‎Au-delà des annonces, le véritable test de cette Semaine mondiale de l’entrepreneuriat sera donc celui des résultats. Le nombre de rencontres et de discours ne suffira pas à mesurer sa réussite. Comme l’a rappelé le représentant des PME, celle-ci devra se traduire par des marchés remportés, des entreprises qui grandissent, des emplois créés et davantage de richesses produites localement. ‎ ‎Thécia Nyomba L’article Semaine mondiale de l'entrepreneuriat : les PME gabonaises réclament des marchés, pas des promesses est apparu en premier sur Gabonreview.com | Actualité du Gabon | .

items.title: Les écologistes Tondelier et Rousseau s’entre-déchirent sur l’alliance avec LFI
items.description: Le conflit entre les deux figures du parti eclate au grand jour a quelques semaines d'un vote interne decisif. Sandrine Rousseau appelle clairement a un ralliement precoce a La France insoumise et a la candidature de Jean-Luc Melenchon largement en tete dans les sondages a gauche , tandis que Marine Tondelier defend sa ligne et son autonomie face a ce qu'elle considere comme des attaques repetees. Un crepage de chignon chez les verts Le 15 novembre sur BFMTV, la deputee de Paris a martele son message : « J'appelle mon parti a rejoindre la dynamique de Jean-Luc Melenchon et la rejoindre tres tot. » Elle estime que la candidature de Marine Tondelier, creditee d'environ 3 %, « doit alimenter une dynamique plus large » et pourrait meme priver la gauche des voix necessaires pour le second tour. « Je la qualifierai meme de dangereuse si elle se maintient », a-t-elle ajoute, annoncant qu'elle ne lui donnerait pas son parrainage. 💬 "Une candidature dangereuse si elle se maintient" Sandrine Rousseau, députée Les Écologistes de Paris, affirme qu'elle ne donnera pas son parrainage à Marine Tondelier, candidate Les Écologistes https://t.co/MTtfTO7B2x — BFM (@BFMTV) November 15, 2026 Marine Tondelier n'a pas tarde a repondre. Sur Franceinfo puis LCI lundi 16 novembre, elle a qualifie ces propos de « provocation ». « Notre mouvement n'est pas une caserne, mais ce n'est pas non plus un self-service sur lequel on peut s'essuyer les pieds sur chaque interview. Qu'on me lâche un peu la grappe et qu'on me laisse faire campagne », a-t-elle lance, jugeant « toxique » la maniere dont l'elue parisienne defend ses idees. « Depuis des annees, elle ne fait pas une interview sans dire du mal de moi », a-t-elle encore souligne, promettant que leur relation « se traitera plus tard, mais se traitera ». ▶️ Présidentielle : Sandrine Rousseau juge la candidature de Marine Tondelier "dangereuse" 🗣️ "Notre mouvement écologiste n’est ni une caserne ni un self-service où l’on peut s’essuyer les pieds à chaque interview. On peut avoir des différends politiques et en débattre en interne, mais on ne peut pas mentir, diffamer et calomnier toute la journée… Qu’on me lâche un peu la grappe et qu’on me laisse faire campagne. La manière dont elle essaie de faire valoir ses idées est toxique." 💬 @marinetondelier, candidate à l’élection présidentielle — LCI (@LCI) November 16, 2026 Cette confrontation s'inscrit dans un contexte deja tendu. Les adherents des ecologistes doivent voter du 10 au 13 decembre pour trancher entre le maintien de la candidature de Marine Tondelier, un soutien a Jean-Luc Melenchon ou un ralliement a Raphael Glucksmann. Sandrine Rousseau juge ce calendrier trop tardif et les modalites peu transparentes. Le depart de Yannick Jadot vers le camp Glucksmann illustre davantage ces fractures . L'ancien candidat ecologiste, suspendu temporairement par son parti apres avoir affiche son soutien a Raphael Glucksmann, est desormais presente comme le « monsieur ecologie » du candidat de Place publique. Il supervise le volet climatique de sa campagne, malgre d'anciennes divergences sur le nucleaire. Cette bascule d'une figure historique vers l'option social-democrate renforce le sentiment d'un parti ecartele entre trois lignes concurrentes, a cinq mois de l'election presidentielle.

items.title: Shenzhen et le Sud global : s’ouvrir au monde, choisir sa voie
items.description: Dans The Shenzhen Mystery (Le Mystère de Shenzhen), l’anthropologue Alan Macfarlane cherche à comprendre la transformation spectaculaire de Shenzhen. Il évoque notamment la rencontre entre des savoir-faire venus d’ailleurs et l’héritage culturel chinois.Ce livre à la main, je suis venue à Shenzhen chercher, dans la ville elle-même, des éléments de réponse. Au pied de la tour Ping An, cette transformation prend une dimension saisissante : près de 600 mètres de haut. À une étape du chantier, sa structure gagnait un étage tous les quatre jours. Voilà la fameuse « vitesse de Shenzhen ». Mais l’essentiel, à mes yeux, n’est pas la hauteur de cette tour, ni même la rapidité de sa construction. C’est ce qui a rendu une telle transformation possible. Comment Shenzhen a-t-elle puisé dans ses échanges avec le monde les moyens de tracer sa propre voie ? Cette question dépasse largement les frontières de la ville. En 1978, Bao’an, le territoire à l’origine de Shenzhen, comptait environ 334 000 habitants. Avec la zone économique spéciale créée en 1980, l’ouverture a attiré investissements et technologies. Aujourd’hui, Shenzhen compte plus de 18 millions d’habitants. Mais surtout, elle a développé ses propres entreprises, ses compétences et tout un écosystème d’innovation. J’ai rencontré ici une équipe de jeunes entrepreneurs. L’un des cofondateurs a 25 ans, et leur moyenne d’âge est inférieure à 30 ans. Tout a commencé par un projet universitaire. Aujourd’hui, ils développent des machines robotisées qui préparent du café et des glaces. Grâce à HarmonyOS, ils relient la prise de commande, la préparation et le service dans un même système. Ils ne se contentent pas de fabriquer des machines. Ils maîtrisent toute une chaîne de compétences. Et c’est précisément ce qui m’intéresse pour le Sud global. Comment participer à l’économie mondiale sans rester cantonné aux activités qui rapportent le moins ? Attirer des investissements ne suffit pas. Il faut regarder ce qu’ils permettent de construire sur place : des ingénieurs formés, des entreprises locales renforcées, des technologies maîtrisées.Sinon, on peut exporter davantage, produire davantage, sans pour autant gagner la maîtrise de son propre développement. Il y a aussi les règles du jeu. Normes numériques, exigences environnementales, accès aux marchés : les pays en développement ne devraient pas simplement appliquer des règles décidées ailleurs. Ils doivent aussi pouvoir participer à leur élaboration, avec l’expertise et les moyens nécessaires. L’APEC peut justement jouer un rôle : favoriser le dialogue, le partage des compétences et une coopération qui élargit les possibilités de chacun. Shenzhen n’est pas un modèle à copier. Chaque pays a son histoire et ses priorités. Mais son expérience nous rappelle une chose essentielle :Le succès de l’ouverture ne se mesure pas seulement au volume des échanges, mais aussi à la capacité de choisir son propre avenir. S’ouvrir au monde, oui. Mais pour mieux choisir sa voie. Shanhui Zhang Présentatrice et chroniqueuse CGTN Français

items.title: UN: 2,230 civilian deaths in Sudan in 10 months, most from drone strikes
items.description: At least 2,230 civilians were killed in Sudan between January and October 2026, including more than 1,630 in drone strikes, according to the UN Human Rights Office. Its latest findings point to the growing role of drones in the war, with attacks increasingly reaching beyond the front lines to strike markets, hospitals, schools, and infrastructure essential to civilian survival. The UN Human Rights Office has confirmed that at least 2,230 civilians were killed in Sudan between January and October, more than 1,630 of them in drone strikes. A report released today says more than 1,390 civilians were killed during the first six months of 2026 in the conflict between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), and allied armed movements. More than 80 per cent of these deaths resulted from drone strikes, which have become a defining feature of the war. In the following four months, a further 840 civilians were killed, including approximately 520 in drone attacks. The UN says these figures cover only cases it has been able to verify, and that the actual civilian death toll is likely to be considerably higher. The report concludes that the continued disregard for the obligation to protect civilians is inflicting an “unbearable toll” on the Sudanese people. Civilians and civilian infrastructure under attack The report, which covers the first half of 2026, documents patterns that have persisted throughout the conflict. These include attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure, indiscriminate strikes, reprisals against people accused of “collaborating” with opposing forces, and the continued use of sexual violence as a weapon of war. It also raises concerns about unlawful killings, arbitrary detention, and the shrinking of civic space. “Battle lines shifted and military tactics – particularly the use of drones – evolved, but the unbearable toll of the war on the Sudanese people has remained as consistent as ever, amid blatant disregard for the protection of civilians,” the report says. UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk (Photo: UN) UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk said: “The facts speak for themselves. The findings in our report provide more evidence, if any were needed, of the ceaselessly unbearable civilian suffering of the war in Sudan and the warring parties’ continued and brazen disregard for the laws of war.” He added: “Amid pervasive impunity, the report documents, once again, serious violations of international humanitarian law. Such violations may amount to war crimes.” Civilians in Kordofan were the worst affected, accounting for more than two-thirds of the verified deaths. Darfur recorded most of the remaining casualties. Eastern and central Sudan were also affected by drone attacks, particularly White Nile state, where at least 41 civilians were killed during the reporting period. Markets, hospitals, schools, fuel supply facilities, water sources, displacement sites, and civilian vehicles were among the targets. Some locations were struck repeatedly. 39 drone strikes on markets During the first half of 2026, the UN Human Rights Office documented at least 39 drone strikes on markets, 20 attacks on civilian vehicles, 17 on fuel tankers and depots, and 16 on healthcare facilities. These attacks raise serious questions about compliance with the laws of war, which protect civilians and civilian objects, including facilities indispensable to the survival of the civilian population. They also raise concerns about the protection of healthcare workers and medical facilities, particularly in areas already desperately short of humanitarian and medical assistance. The report says drone attacks on markets, combined with looting and restrictions on movement, have severely disrupted access to food. In October, the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) warned that conflict, displacement, and drought were increasing the risk of famine in parts of Darfur and Kordofan, as acute food insecurity and malnutrition continued to rise. October also saw a high number of civilian casualties, alongside an escalation in drone attacks on civilian infrastructure, with devastating consequences for the population. Attacks on power and fuel infrastructure Among the most concerning developments is the recent escalation in drone attacks targeting power generation facilities and fuel supplies. In just over two weeks, between 20 October and 4 November, 29 drone strikes attributed to the RSF targeted electricity infrastructure and fuel depots in 11 states. The attacks caused widespread power cuts and worsened fuel shortages, affecting millions of people far from the front lines. The consequences for civilians and essential services have been severe. Power cuts have disrupted healthcare, including kidney dialysis and surgical procedures, while also restricting access to clean water and food production. The report stresses that accountability, regardless of the perpetrators’ affiliation, is essential to breaking cycles of violence and preventing further violations and abuses. Türk called on all parties to the conflict to protect civilians and fulfil their obligations under international law. “The world is watching,” he said. Share article The post UN: 2,230 civilian deaths in Sudan in 10 months, most from drone strikes appeared first on Dabanga Radio TV Online .
